title: Atukula laddu
subtitle: Flaky Rice Laddu
procedure: Clean flaky rice and grind it in a food processor/mixie into coarse powder.
Grate jaggery and coconut and keep the contents aside separately.
Roast cashew nuts and raisins in ghee.
Boil milk and add jaggery powder to it and mix the contents well.
Add the jaggery mixed boiled milk in the ground flaky rice and mix the contents well.
Make lemon-sized balls from the mixture while it is still hot.
Stick one cashew nut and one raisin in each of the balls.

title: Carrot Halwa
subtitle: Carrot Halwa
procedure: Wash carrots thoroughly and peel them. Grate them and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp ghee to it.
When ghee is heated, fry cashew nuts and raisins and keep the contents aside.
Add the remaining ghee and fry the grated carrot for 5 minutes.
Add milk to the contents and reduce the flame.
Stir the contents continuously till the entire milk gets evaporated.
Add sugar and cardamom powder to the dried content and mix well.
When the sugar syrup thickens, add fried cashew nuts and raisins and put off the flame.

title: Atukula payasam
subtitle: Flaky Rice Pudding

ingredients.name: Custard powder / All purpose flour / wheat flour

procedure: Place a thick-bottomed vessel and boil milk in it.
Add sugar to it and boil for 10 minutes. Cool 1 cup of this milk.
Mix custard powder in 1 cup of boiled and cooled milk. Stir the contents regularly and see that no lumps are formed.
Add the custard contents to boiling milk and stir the contents for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and add flaky rice to the contents.
Roast cashew nuts and raisins in ghee and mix them in the Payasam.
Garnish the dish with grated coconut and cardamom powder and serve.

title: Sweet Undrallu
subtitle: Sweet With Rice-Flour And Coconut
procedure: Grate coconut and keep aside.
Grate a block of jaggery into a thick bottomed frying pan and mix it along with cardamom powder and grated coconut. Place this pan on flame.
Constantly stir the contents on low-flame.
After 10 minutes, take a small quantity of the mixture on to a small plate and test with fingers that it can be made into a ball.
If the mixture does not stick together to form ball, let the contents remain on flame for another 5 minutes and continue stirring until required consistency is obtained.
Add cardamom powder to the mixture, mix well and remove from flame.
Once cooled, make the mixture into small balls smaller than lemon size.
Place another thick-bottomed vessel on flame and add 2 glasses of water to it.
When the water is boiling, reduce flame to low/medium, add rice flour and mix well. Take off the flame.
Once cooled, by sprinkling water as necessary, mix the contents well.
Prepare rice flour balls that are little bigger than lemon-sized. Pat these balls into small-sized flat pancakes with palms. Using wet palms helps this process considerably.
Place each coconut ball in the middle of the rice flour pancakes and wrap the pancake around the coconut ball and press edges till the coconut balls are enclosed on all sides.
After all the balls have been prepared, place these balls in a pressure cooker and cook them without cooker-weight just like Idlies for 15 minutes and take off from the flame.
Once cooled, gently lift the balls and place them onto a fresh plate. See to it that the balls are not broken.
note: These are also prepared during Ganesh chaturthi festival and offered to Lord Ganesh.

title: Chakkera Pongali
subtitle: Rice and Moong Dal Pudding

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram dal without skin
Sugar or Jaggery
ingredients.quantity: 1 cup sugar or ¼ kg jaggery

procedure: Clean rice and moong dal. Fry these separately for 5 minutes in a deep frying pan along with 1 tsp ghee.
Add 3 cups of water and cook rice and moong dal together. Once cooked, add either sugar or jaggery to it; if sugar is added, rice may turn a bit thin and stir frequently on low flame.
Grate the coconut and add to the rice.
In another pan, fry cashew nuts and raisins in ghee. Pour this onto the rice and add cardamom powder.
When rice becomes thick after a while, add ghee and take off from the flame.
note: Some prefer adding milk to this, but this will once again become 'Payasam'. Therefore, the above mentioned procedure is the only method to prepare 'Chakkera Pongali'. Instead of a pressure cooker, a rice cooker may also be utilized.

title: Biyyam Payasam
subtitle: Rice Pudding
procedure: Clean rice and add 4 cups of water. Place this in a pressure cooker and cook till the rice becomes soft slightly over-cooked.
Add jaggery to the rice and cook on a low-flame for 5 minutes while stirring frequently.
When the jaggery gets completely dissolved in the rice, remove the vessel from flame.
Add boiled milk and cardamom powder. Mix well and serve.
Cashew nuts and raisins may also be added to the Payasam.
note: Rice should only be cooked with water, as cooking rice with milk may turn it sour after adding jaggery. Full fat milk should be used; using skim or low-fat milk detracts from the taste. This is made usually on important festivals and during religious ceremonies.

title: Semya Payasam
subtitle: Vermicelli Pudding
procedure: Roast vermicelli in 2 tsp ghee till golden brown.
Roast cashew nuts and raisins in ghee and keep aside.
In a vessel pour 3 cups of water and put it on flame. When the water is boiling, add roasted vermicelli to the water and reduce the flame. Stir this continuously.
When vermicelli is cooked, add sugar and stir it again till the mixture becomes thick.
Add boiled milk — milk should be boiled separately beforehand.
Add cardamom powder, cashew nuts and raisins and mix well.
note: Vermicelli can also be cooked with milk but for this, another ½ liter of milk will be required. Using skim or low-fat milk instead of full-fat milk detracts from the taste.

title: Rava Laddu
subtitle: Semolina Laddu

ingredients.name: Semolina (Bombay rava or Sooji, not rice or idli rava)

procedure: Place a thick bottomed pan on flame. Add 2 tsp of ghee and roast cashew nuts and raisins one after the other.
In the same pan, add another 2 tsp of ghee and roast semolina till it turns golden brown in color.
Boil the milk separately.
Grind sugar in a food processor/blender/mixer for a few seconds and add this powdered sugar to the roasted semolina.
Add boiled milk and cardamom powder. Mix this well.
Make lemon-sized balls from the mixture while it is still hot. Stick one cashew nut and one raisin in each of the balls.
note: Once cooled, store in a container. This will be fresh up to a week.

title: Kobbari Nauju
subtitle: Caramelized Grated Coconut
procedure: Break coconuts and grate them.
Grate jaggery separately.
Put a thick bottomed vessel on flame and add grated coconut and jaggery together.
Set the flame on low/medium.
Mix the contents frequently.
After 10 minutes, take a bit of the contents and touch it with fingers. If it is sticky enough to prepare into balls then remove the vessel from the flame.
If it does not form balls, let the contents remain on flame for some more time and continue stirring till the required consistency is obtained.
Before removing from flame, add cardamom powder and mix.
Once the contents are half-cooled, prepare lemon-sized balls and store in a dry container.
note: These balls can be stored for 10 to 15 days.

title: Kobbari Payasam
subtitle: Coconut Pudding
procedure: Soak rice in water for 4 hours.
Break coconut and cut into small pieces.
Grind the soaked rice along with coconut pieces into a smooth paste adding ½ cup water.
In 4 cups of water, add jaggery or sugar and put this on low-medium flame.
When the jaggery is completely dissolved in the water, add the above mentioned paste to the water. Stir continuously; see to it that no lumps are formed.
Cook this for 10 minutes and then add cardamom powder and mix well.
In a pan, roast cashew nuts and raisins in ghee and pour this onto the Payasam.
note: See to it that the payasam is neither too thick nor too thin; according to its consistency, add water. This can either be consumed hot or cold after placing it in a refrigerator.

title: Ragula Halwa
subtitle: Finger Millet Sweet Halwa
procedure: Add water to the finger millet flour and prepare it into batter similar to preparing dosas.
Add it to a deep and thick-bottomed vessel and cook it on low/medium flame.
Reduce the flame and stir the contents frequently.
When the batter turns thick, add sugar and ghee to the contents and stir the contents frequently.
In another pan, fry cashew nuts and raisins in ghee. Pour these onto the thick batter.
Add cardamom powder to the contents and mix well.
Grease a steel-plate with ghee and pour the whole content into it. Spread the thick paste evenly. When half-cooled, cut the paste into 1-inch pieces.
note: This dish is quite healthy and nutritious for children.

title: Ragula Payasam
subtitle: Finger Millet Pudding
procedure: Wash finger millets thoroughly and soak in water for at least 10 hours.
Drain water completely and tie them tightly in a dry cloth and let it sprout.
Grind them the next day in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Grind coconut in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
In another pan, fry cashew nuts and raisins in ghee and keep them aside.
Place a thick-bottomed vessel on low/medium flame and boil milk.
Add the ground finger millets and coconut together to the boiled milk.
Stir the contents frequently and see to it that no lumps are formed.
When fully cooked, add sugar to the contents and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add fried cashew nuts and raisins to the contents along with cardamom powder and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: The dish can also be consumed after refrigeration. If you want to prepare Payasam with sprouted finger millets, plan it 2 days in advance. Sprouted millets are good for health and have many nutritional values. If you want to prepare it instantly, use finger millet flour for preparation.

title: Bobbatlu
subtitle: Sweet Chapatti

ingredients.name: Chana dal / yellow chick pea flour

procedure: Sieve maida and atta and knead these together into thick dough by adding water gradually; the quantity of water should be slightly more than required to prepare Chapattis. The dough should be soft, but not too thin.
Cover the wet flour with a lid and keep it aside for at least 2 hours. Form 1½–2 inch balls from the dough.
Cook chana dal with water in a pressure cooker. Once cooked, drain the entire water from it and add jaggery.
Grind Yellow Chick Pea Flour and jaggery together into a smooth paste and add cardamom powder to it.
Add the paste to a thick bottomed pan and put it on low flame. Regularly stir the contents for 10 minutes till it turns thick.
Take a small portion of the thick paste and by applying ghee on to a palm, roll this into 1-inch balls and keep aside.
Spread the flour balls in a palm and place the Yellow Chick Pea Flour balls into it and close the flour from all sides around the ball.
Apply ghee on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag or a banana leaf if available) and place the stuffed balls on it and spread it out into thin round chapattis by using fingers.
Place a pan on flame and spread a small quantity of ghee on it.

Gently transfer the spread-out chapatti on to the pan along with the polythene bag/banana leaf and slowly peel off the bag/leaf away from the flame. Place chapatti in such a way that it sticks to the pan and the leaf/bag is placed above the chapatti.
note: See to it that the chapatti does not get torn while peeling it off from the leaf/polythene bag.

title: Kobbari Halwa
subtitle: Coconut Halwa
procedure: Grate the coconut.
In a thick bottomed vessel, add grated coconut and sugar and place the vessel on low-medium flame. Stir the contents continuously.
When the contents turn thick, add ghee and cardamom powder and let the vessel remain on flame for 3 more minutes and then take off the flame.
Grease a steel-plate with ghee and pour the whole contents into it. Spread the thick paste evenly.
When half-cooled, cut the paste into 1-inch pieces and store it in a container.
note: This can be stored for a week to 10 days.

title: Appaalu
subtitle: Sweet Vadas
procedure: Pour 2 cups of water in a thick-bottomed vessel and mix jaggery powder. Place this vessel on low-medium flame.
When jaggery gets completely dissolved in water, add grated coconut to the rice flour and mix this with the jaggery water. Add cardamom powder and stir.
Reduce the flame and stir frequently.
Take off the flame and let the contents cool for 3 minutes.
On a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag or a banana leaf if available), spread a small amount of the above mixture and shape into 'Vadas' with fingers — these should be about 2 inches in diameter.
Fry these Vadas in oil.
note: These can be consumed hot or cold. The dish can be prepared easily but should be consumed immediately as it does not store well.

title: Ariselu
subtitle: Rice Pancake
procedure: Soak rice for 5 to 6 hours and then wash it. Spread the rice on a dry cloth and let it dry in shade for ½ hour.
Grind the dried rice into flour in a food processor/mixer.
Grate jaggery into a thick bottomed vessel, preferably a brass vessel, and add ½ glass of water to it. Place the vessel on low/medium flame and stir the contents regularly.
Within 10 minutes, the contents would turn into thick syrup with a consistency that it can be rolled into balls.

Gradually pour the ground rice flour into the syrup along with sesame seeds and stir regularly. This could be best prepared when 2 people work on this — one can pour the flour and the other can simultaneously stir the contents.
See to it that the resultant paste is neither too thick nor thin. The end result should be that the paste should not be too thick.
Place another vessel on a medium/high flame and pour most of the oil into it.

Apply a bit of the left over oil on a polythene bag and roll a small portion of the thick paste into small chapattis — about 3–4 inches in diameter. Traditionally a banana leaf is used in place of the polythene bag.
Fry these chapattis when the oil is hot and remove them with a spatula and press each of the chapattis till the oil is completely drained off.
Fry all the chapattis in the same manner one-by-one and drain oil from each one of them.
Place these on a paper towel till they cool; otherwise they tend to stick to each other. Then store them in a container.
note: To check jaggery syrup consistency: pour water in a small plate, drop a small quantity of syrup into it, see that the drop does not dissolve in water. Take it between fingers and try to form into balls — if balls can be formed, the consistency is right; if not, continue stirring and keep testing till a ball can be formed.

title: Besan Laddu
subtitle: Yellow Chick Pea Flour Laddu

ingredients.name: Besan / chana dal / split yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Fry besan flour in half a cup of ghee for 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat the remaining ghee separately in another pan.
Add sugar and cardamom powder to the besan flour and mix well.
Pour heated ghee into the flour and mix well with a ladle.
When still hot, roll the flour into lemon-sized balls.
note: These can be stored for 15 days without refrigeration.

title: Pesarapappu Halwa
subtitle: Mung Bean Halwa
procedure: Clean moong dal and sauté/roast it till golden brown without oil.
Mix with water and grind it into paste. Add water slowly until mung bean turns into thick paste. Typically about 1 cup of water would be required.
In a thick bottomed vessel, put ½ cup of water and add sugar and place it on a low/medium flame. Stir this regularly till the sugar syrup becomes slightly sticky.
Pour the paste into the syrup and stir it regularly.
Add ghee and continue stirring.
When the paste turns thick, add cardamom powder.
When the paste reaches a consistency that it starts leaving the sides of the pan, switch off the flame.
Grease a steel plate with ghee and pour the cooked thick paste and pat to the same thickness across the paste.
Cut the paste into pieces about 1 inch squares.
Fry cashew nuts and raisins till golden brown in 2 tsp ghee and keep aside.
Stick fried cashew nuts and raisins on the squares.

title: Minapasunni
subtitle: Block Gram Laddu

ingredients.name: Urad dal / block gram white without skin

procedure: Sauté/roast urad dal without oil in a frying pan till it turns golden brown.
When cooled, grind it into fine powder in a food processor/mixer and keep it aside.
Add jaggery powder or sugar to it.
Heat ghee in a pan and when hot, pour it into the flour and jaggery mixture and mix well.
Roll the flour into lemon-sized balls while still hot.
note: These balls can be stored for up to a month.

title: Ravvakesari
subtitle: Semolina Halwa
procedure: In a thick-bottomed pan, pour 2 tsp of ghee and fry cashew nuts and then raisins separately and keep them aside.
In another pan, pour 2 tsp of ghee and fry semolina till it turns golden brown.
Place a thick bottomed pan on flame and add 6 cups of water.
At the point of boiling, gradually pour semolina and regularly stir.
Reduce the flame. After 5 minutes, add sugar and mix the contents. Stir continuously so that no lumps are formed.
Sugar gets dissolved in the paste and makes the paste thin.
When it starts to thicken again, add remaining ghee and mix well.
When ghee gets completely mixed with the paste, add cashew nuts, raisins and cardamom powder. Mix the whole contents again thoroughly. Remove from flame.
note: The dish can also be served in pieces — grease a steel-plate with ghee, pour the cooked semolina paste into it, and when cooled, cut into 1-inch square pieces. Saffron can also be added as per preference; if adding saffron, add 3–4 sprigs into the water in step 3.

title: Kajjikayalu
subtitle: Dry Coconut And Yellow Chickpea Flour Sweet
procedure: Cut the dry coconut into small ½ inch pieces. Add 2 tsp of cooking oil in a pan and fry/roast till golden brown.
Once cooled, grind the roasted coconut into powder in a food processor/mixer.
In a pan, sauté chana dal flour and sesame seeds separately without oil. After cooling, grind them separately into powder in a food processor/mixer.
Grate jaggery (sugar can also be used).
Mix all the powdered contents along with jaggery and cardamom powder and keep it aside.
Sieve maida flour. Add water gradually and knead till it becomes thick dough similar to preparing 'Puri' dough or similar to bread dough.
Roll the dough into ½ inch balls and then roll them out into 3–4 inch diameter circles same as the shape of puris.
Place one spoon of powdered mixture called 'Purnam' in the middle of the puri and wrap the puri in an elliptical shape and press edges till the sweet powder is enclosed on all sides.
After preparing a few numbers of 'Kajjikayas', place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame with oil and heat it.
Fry 'Kajjikayas' in the heated oil till they turn into golden brown.
Prepare the entire dish in the same procedure.
note: Roll 3–4 kajjikayas, fry them and repeat the process. If all the kajjikayas are rolled out first and then fried, the stuffing may come out of some of the sealed kajjikayas due to exposure to moisture. These can be stored for 15 days. This item is usually prepared during the Diwali festival.

title: Chandrakantalu
subtitle: Mung Bean Halwa

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram dal without skin

procedure: Soak moong dal for 4 hours in water. Drain all the water and grind it into smooth paste without adding any water.
Add sugar to the paste. Pour this mixture into a thick bottomed vessel and place on a low/medium flame. Stir continuously.
Initially the paste will become thin but will gradually turn thick when stirred regularly.
Add cardamom powder and mix well.

Take a small quantity of the paste into another plate and touch it with your fingers. The right consistency is reached if it does not stick to the fingers. Keep stirring till the right consistency is reached.
Grease a steel-plate with ghee and transfer the paste into it. Once cooled, cut the paste into 1–2 inch square pieces.
Place a pan on flame and add oil. When oil is heated, deep fry these pieces till golden brown.
note: These can be consumed either hot or cold.

title: Purnam Boorelu
subtitle: Split Yellow Chickpea Flour Sweet

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Soak rice and urad dal in water for at least 5–6 hours.
Drain water completely and grind it in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste. It should be of the consistency similar to Dosa batter.
Add baking powder to the ground paste and keep it aside for 1 hour.
Cook chana dal flour in a pressure cooker by adding water to it. For 1 cup of chana dal flour, add 2 cups of water.
Drain water from the contents.
Add jaggery and cardamom powder to the cooked chana dal flour and grind it in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame and add the ground chana dal flour contents.
Stir the contents continuously for 10 minutes.
When the contents turn thick, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Make this into small sized balls and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, dip each ball in the prepared batter and drop them in the oil.
Fry the balls till they turn into golden brown.
Prepare all the balls in the same manner.
note: It tastes better when consumed with ghee. The dish should be consumed immediately, as it does not store well.

title: Kobbari Annam
subtitle: Coconut Rice

ingredients.name: Seasoning: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Clean rice thoroughly and cook it; see to it that the rice is non-sticky.
Grate coconut and keep it aside.
Spread the cooked rice in a wide plate and add half quantity of oil and mix well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the seasoning ingredients.
Add green chillies and curry leaves to the fried contents and fry for 1 minute.
Put off the flame and add the fried contents to the cooked rice and mix well.
In a thick-bottomed pan, pour the remaining 2 tsp of ghee and fry cashew nuts and then raisins separately and add them to the cooked contents.
Add salt and grated coconut to the rice and mix the contents well.
note: Serve the contents after 1 hour of preparation to taste better.

title: Rajma Rice
subtitle: Kidney Beans Rice
procedure: Soak kidney beans for 5–6 hours in 4 cups of water and then cook them.
Cook rice separately and keep it aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry green chillies.
Add onion pieces and ginger-garlic paste to the contents and fry well.
Add cooked kidney beans and rice to the contents and mix well.
Add salt and garam masala powder to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: It tastes better when consumed with 'Raita' (Perugupaccadi). Rajma is good for health.

title: Mamidikaya Pulihora
subtitle: Mango Rice

ingredients.name: Seasoning: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Wash rice thoroughly and add 4 cups of water to it.
Add turmeric powder and cook the rice. See to it that rice does not stick.
Peel mangoes and cut them into small pieces.
Add salt to mango pieces and grind in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Spread the cooked rice in a wide plate and add half the quantity of oil and the ground mango paste and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies, split chana dal flour, urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add green chillies and curry leaves to the fried contents and fry for 1 minute.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared rice and mix the contents well.
Add asafoetida in 1 tsp water and add it to the prepared rice and mix the contents well.
note: Place a lid over the prepared contents to get fine aroma. Cook rice in such a way that it does not stick or use non-sticky/long-grain rice.

title: Pulagam
subtitle: Mung Bean Rice

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram dal without skin

procedure: Wash rice and moong dal together.
Add 4½ cups water, salt and turmeric powder. Fry cumin seeds in ghee and pour it on the rice.
Put the rice vessel in a pressure cooker and let it remain on flame for up to 3 whistles. Take away from the flame.
note: This is offered as Prasadam to Goddess Parvati during festivals. It tastes better when consumed with ghee and 'Avakaya' Mango pickle.

title: Pulihora
subtitle: Tamarind Rice

ingredients.name: Seasoning: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Clean rice and cook it.
Mix salt, turmeric powder and asafoetida to a cup of tamarind puree and keep it aside.
Spread the cooked rice in a wide plate and add ½ cup of oil and tamarind puree to this and mix well.
Place a thick bottomed pan with oil on medium flame. When it is hot, roast chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, red dried chillies and peanuts and fry till mustard seeds splutter.
Add green chillies and curry leaves and fry this for 2 minutes.
Pour the seasoning on rice and mix well.
note: It tastes better when consumed 1 to 2 hours after its preparation. This is also an ideal food while traveling since it does not require refrigeration for up to 2 days. Cook rice in such a way that it does not stick or use non-sticky/long-grain rice.

title: Vegetable Pulav
subtitle: Vegetable Pulav
procedure: Wash rice thoroughly and add 4 cups of water to the contents and cook rice.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add half the quantity of oil.
When oil is heated, add thoroughly washed vegetable pieces to it.
Add salt to the content and mix well.
Place a lid over the vessel and stir the contents frequently.
When the vegetables are fully cooked, add the cooked rice to the contents and mix well.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining quantity of oil in it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry ginger-garlic paste.
Add garam masala powder and masala leaves to the fried paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add the contents to the cooked rice and mix the contents well.
note: It tastes better when consumed with 'Ullipaya perugupaccadi'. The dish can also be prepared using plain rice instead of Basmati rice; however, cook rice in such a way that it does not stick or use non-sticky/long-grain rice.

title: Bangaladumpa Parota
subtitle: Chapattis Stuffed With Potatoes
procedure: Wash potatoes thoroughly and peel their skin.
Cook potatoes in water. Do not cook in a pressure cooker.
When cooled, mash potatoes using hands.
Add salt, red chilli powder, garam masala powder and finely chopped curry leaves to the mashed potatoes and mix the contents well.
Add atta to mashed potatoes and knead into thick dough. Use water only if necessary.
Immediately begin preparing chapattis without allowing the atta to dry.
Take a small portion of atta-potato mixture and spread it out into small round chapattis using a rolling pin as in normal rotis/chapattis — gives best results.
Cook chapattis on a flat pan on low/medium flame. Turn them over frequently. When almost cooked, add oil or ghee as per taste on both the sides and remove from flame.
note: This preparation goes well with 'ullipaya perugupaccadi'. To serve with raita: add salt to fresh curd/yogurt, finely chop onions, ripened tomatoes and coriander leaves, add them to the curd/yogurt and mix well, serve with chapattis.

title: Mullangi Parota
subtitle: Chapatti Stuffed With Radish
procedure: Wash radish thoroughly and peel it. After peeling, grate it and add salt to the contents.
Completely drain water from the grated radish by squeezing it using hands.
Finely chop green chillies and coriander leaves and add them to the grated radish.
Mix the contents well and keep aside.
Knead atta into thick dough by adding water gradually — the dough should be prepared similar to preparing the dough for chapattis. It should be soft, but not too thin.
Take a small portion of the thick paste, roll this into 1-inch balls and spread it out into thin round chapattis by using rolling pin.
Place the contents of the grated radish into it and place another spread out chapatti prepared as above on top of it.
Close the ends of both the chapattis together on all sides and gently press the ends using rolling pin.
Fry the stuffed chapatti on a pan without oil on a low/medium flame, repeatedly turning it over so that it cooks well on both sides.
When almost completely fried, apply a small amount of oil (quarter tsp) on each side, turn over two more times on each side, remove from flame, and serve.
note: This goes well with any kind of 'curd chutnies/raitas' or 'bellam avakaya'.

title: Menthikoora Parotalu
subtitle: Chapattis With Fenugreek Leaves
procedure: Remove stalks of fenugreek leaves and clean them.
Finely chop the leaves and wash them thoroughly.
Add chopped leaves to the atta and add salt, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala powder.
Mix all the contents and knead atta into thick dough by adding water gradually. Keep the kneaded dough aside for 10 minutes.
Take small portions of the thick paste and roll them into thin round parothas.

Place a pan on flame and fry the parothas frequently flipping them on both sides. When almost fully cooked, apply a few drops of oil on each side, flip on each side for two more times and remove from flame.
note: This dish should be served hot.

title: Masala Garelu
subtitle: Spicy Vadas With Mixed Dal

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chick pea flour

procedure: Soak split chana dal and the remaining dals separately in water for 4–5 hours.
Wash them thoroughly. Take half the quantity of split chana dal and add the remaining dals and green chillies to the contents.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Finely chop onions and curry leaves and add them to the ground paste.
Add salt and cumin seeds to the paste and mix well.
Add the remaining split chana dal content and apply water on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag); place a lemon-sized content of the prepared batter and press it into the shape of vadas.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop each such vada in the oil and fry till they turn into golden brown.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Kobbari Vadalu
subtitle: Coconut Vadas
procedure: Grate coconut and keep it aside.
Add maida and rice flour to the grated coconut.
Add 1½ cups of water to a thick-bottomed vessel and place it on medium/high flame.
Grind green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste and add it to the boiling water.
Add 1 tsp oil and grated coconut mixture to the boiling water and mix well.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Apply oil on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag) and place lemon-sized balls on it and spread it out into small, round vadas by using fingers — these should be about 2 inches in diameter.
Fry these vadas in oil.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Carrot Cutlet
subtitle: Carrot Cutlet
procedure: Wash carrot and beetroot thoroughly and peel their skins.
Grate carrot and beetroot and keep the contents aside.
Chop green chillies into small pieces.
Crush dried bread crumbs into fine powder and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry green chillies.
Add grated carrot and beetroot contents and add salt to it.
Place a lid over the vessel and cook the contents on low flame.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time and sprinkle water as necessary.
Once cooked, sprinkle garam masala powder and put off the flame.
Once cooled, prepare oval-shaped balls of the contents.
Prepare thin batter by mixing besan flour with water.
Dip the balls in the batter and then roll them in the crushed dried bread crumbs.
Prepare all the balls in the same manner.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, deep fry the prepared balls.
note: See to it that before frying the contents, oil should be very hot. Do not stir Pakodis immediately after dropping the balls into the hot oil — stir only when they are fried well to avoid breakage.

title: Atukula Pulihora
subtitle: Spicy Flaky Rice

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Clean flaky rice and wash it thoroughly with water.
Drain water completely and put a lid over the contents and keep it aside for 1 hour.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry split chana dal, urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add green chillies, dried red chilli, curry leaves and peanuts to the contents and fry for 5 minutes.
Add flaky rice to the fried contents and fry for 4 minutes.
In a small bowl, add salt, turmeric powder and asafoetida to lemon juice and mix well.
Add the lemon juice contents to the flaky rice and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: For preparing pulihora, use chudva flaky rice instead of thick flaky rice for better results.

title: Bobbarla Garelu
subtitle: Black Eyed Beans Vadas
procedure: Soak black eyed beans in water 4–5 hours.
Finely chop onions into small pieces.
Wash black beans thoroughly and add half the quantity of onions, green chillies, ginger, cumin seeds and salt.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste without adding water.
Add the remaining onion pieces to the ground batter and mix the contents well.
Place a lemon-sized content of the prepared batter on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag) and press it into the shape of vadas.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop each such vada in the oil and fry till they turn into golden brown and serve.

title: Chitti Boorelu
subtitle: Small Cake Buns
procedure: Mix maida, rice flour and baking powder together in buttermilk and make it into thick batter as in the case of Pakodies.
Keep the contents aside for 4 hours.
Grind green chillies, cumin seeds and salt in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste and add it to the soaked contents.
Place a thick bottomed pan and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop ½ a tsp full of batter in the oil similar to making pakodis — drop small quantity of batter, as oil may bubble up and overflow.
Reduce the flame to low and fry the boorelu till they turn into golden brown.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour. It tastes better when consumed hot. (Note: boorelu = kind of pakodis)

title: Perugu Garelu
subtitle: Vadas In Curd/Yogurt
procedure: Soak urad dal in water for at least 5–6 hours.
When soaked, wash the contents thoroughly and add salt to the contents.
Grind the content in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste without adding water.
Place a lemon-sized content of the prepared batter on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag) and press it into the shape of thin, round vadas.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop each such vada in the oil and fry till they turn into golden brown and serve.
note: You can add chopped cabbage, onions and green chillies to the ground batter to prepare cabbage vadas/garelu. You can also add these vadas without cabbage to curd/yogurt by adding fried seasoning as described in avada recipe to make perugu garelu/avadas.

title: Upma
subtitle: Semolina Upma
procedure: Dry roast semolina in a pan on low flame till light golden, stirring continuously. Keep aside.
Place a deep pan on low/medium flame, add oil.
When oil is heated, add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add urad dal, chana dal and cashew nuts and fry till golden.
Add green chillies, ginger and curry leaves and fry for 1 minute.
Add chopped onions and fry till translucent.
Add 4 cups of water and salt and bring to a boil.
Slowly add the roasted semolina to the boiling water while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Reduce flame, cover and cook for 3–4 minutes till semolina absorbs the water and is fully cooked.
Mix well and serve hot.
note: Bombay rava (coarse semolina) gives the best texture; avoid rice rava or idli rava. Tastes well with coconut chutney or pickle.

title: Avada
subtitle: Curd-Vadas / Dahi Vadas
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Put off the flame and add the contents to the curd/yogurt.
Add salt, turmeric powder, finely chopped coriander leaves and green chillies to the content and mix well.
Add the fried vadas to the prepared curd/yogurt.
note: It tastes better when consumed 2–3 hours after the preparation.

title: Perugu Bondalu
subtitle: Bonda With Buttermilk
procedure: Add maida flour, rice flour, salt and baking powder in sour buttermilk and prepare it into a consistency similar to preparing pakodas and soak the contents for 4–5 hours.
Grind green chillies and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Add the contents to the prepared batter.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop the batter similar to preparing pakodis in the heated oil and fry till golden brown.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour. It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Ullipaya Pakodi
subtitle: Onion Pakoda
procedure: Peel onions and cut them into small pieces.
Grind ginger, green chillies and salt in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
In a wide plate, mix besan flour, rice flour, onion pieces, green chilli paste, baking powder and salt together and add water to the contents.
Knead the contents into a thick batter.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop 1 tsp of prepared batter into the oil and fry till they turn into golden brown in color.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot. Finely chopped cabbage can also be added to the batter for preparing Pakodis.

title: Goruchikkudu Pakodi
subtitle: Cluster Beans Pakoda
procedure: Peel onions and chop them into small pieces.
Grind green chillies, ginger and salt into smooth paste.
Mix besan flour, rice flour, baking powder, green chilli paste, cluster bean pieces, onions and red chilli powder together into smooth batter by adding water as necessary.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop teaspoon full of batter into the oil and deep fry.
In the same manner use the entire batter to prepare Pakodis.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Chakrabanalu
subtitle: Salted Plain Flour Chips
procedure: Sieve maida flour and add it to a wide plate.
Grind salt and ajwain in a food processor/mixie into fine powder and add it to the maida flour.
Add ghee to the contents and mix well.
Add water to the contents and knead it into a smooth batter similar to preparing chapattis. Do not soak the contents.
Immediately after kneading the batter, take a lemon-sized ball of the batter and spread it out into thin, round chapattis.
Cut the chapattis into 1-inch pieces using knife.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the chapatti pieces in the oil till they turn into golden brown; place them on a tissue paper to absorb excessive oil.
Prepare the entire batter in the same manner and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, store the contents in a dry container.
note: This is very healthy for kids. As the dish contains ajwain, it hinders indigestion. The dish stays fresh for 15 days.

title: Jantikalu
subtitle: Mixed Flour Vermicelli

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds / til seeds without skin

procedure: Sieve rice flour and wheat flour together into a wide plate.
Add salt and sesame seeds to the contents.
Heat ghee and pour it into the contents.
Add water and knead the contents into thick batter.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.

When oil is heated, reduce the flame and drop the batter using the jantikala gottam equipment to prepare jantikalau. A special equipment called 'jantikalu – jantikala gottam' is available in many stores.
Fry the contents till they turn into golden brown.
Prepare the entire contents in the same manner and let the contents cool.
Store the contents in a dry container and tightly place a lid over the container.
note: It stays fresh for up to 15 days. It can be consumed during tea time or fed to children after they return from school. Use a big-holed plate of the equipment for preparing jantikalu.

title: Instant Jantikalu
subtitle: Rice Flour Vermicelli

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds / til seeds without skin

procedure: Place a thick-bottomed vessel with 2 cups water on medium/high flame.
Add 2 cups of cold water to rice flour and mix the contents well.
When water is boiling, add the rice flour to the water and stir continuously; see that no lumps are formed.
When the flour is cooked well, add ground green chilli, salt and cumin seed paste to the contents.
Add sesame seeds to the contents and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, use the jantikala gottam equipment to make jantikalau. A special equipment called 'jantikalu – jantikala gottam' is available in many stores.
Prepare jantikalu of requisite size and shape and place them on a polythene sheet and sun-dry the contents.
When fully dried, store them in a container with care.
note: The same paste can be used for preparing small 'vadiyalu'. As required, fry jantikalu in heated oil and serve.

title: Kaarappoosa
subtitle: Thin Spiced Vermicelli
procedure: Sieve besan flour and add red chilli powder and baking powder to the contents.
Grind ajwain and salt in a food processor/mixie into fine powder and add them to the contents.
Add water to the contents and knead the dough into thick batter.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.

When oil is heated, reduce the flame and drop the batter using the jantikala gottam equipment. Stuff the batter up to half of the equipment and by pressing hard, drop the batter into the heated oil and fry.
Fry the contents till they turn into golden brown.
Prepare the entire contents in the same manner and let the contents cool.
Store the contents in a dry container and tightly place a lid over the container.
note: It stays fresh for up to 1 month. Do not store while the contents are still hot as it may develop vapor that make the contents soft. Use only fresh cooking oil for preparing snack items. For preparing kaarappoosa, use narrow holed plate of the jantikala gottam equipment.

title: Mokkajonnala Pakodi
subtitle: Corn Pakoda
procedure: Separate corn seeds from corns and wash them thoroughly.
Grind them in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Add salt, onions, cumin seeds and green chillies to the paste and grind the contents into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop 1 tsp of ground paste into the oil and deep fry the contents.
Similarly, fry the entire contents and serve.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Uppupindi
subtitle: Upma With Rice Ravva

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram without skin
Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Cut ginger and green chillies into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal and mustard seeds.
Add ginger, green chilli pieces and curry leaves to the contents and fry for 1 minute.
Add 5 cups of water, moong dal and salt and place a lid over the contents.
When water starts boiling, add rice ravva and grated coconut and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and transfer the contents to a thick-bottomed vessel.
Cook the contents in a pressure cooker and cook for 3 whistles.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: Rice ravva is available in supermarkets and could also be prepared at home. Use non-sticky/long-grain rice for the preparation. To prepare rice ravva at home: wash rice thoroughly with water and drain water completely, keep the wet rice aside for 2 hours, sun-dry the contents and when fully dried, grind in a food processor/mixie into coarse ravva, then sieve ravva and segregate flour from it.

title: Semiya Upma
subtitle: Vermicelli Upma

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Sauté/roast vermicelli in 1 tsp oil in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Finely chop onions, green chillies and ginger into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry chana dal, urad dal and mustard seeds till the dals turn golden brown.
Add green chillies, onions, ginger and curry leaves and fry them for 1 minute.
Add 3 cups of water, salt and cashew nuts to the contents and place a lid over the vessel.
When water starts to boil, add vermicelli and mix the contents well.
Replace the lid over the contents and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and add lemon juice and serve.

title: Cabbage Pakodi
subtitle: Cabbage Pakoda
procedure: Chop green chillies and curry leaves into small pieces.
Mix besan flour, rice flour, green chillies, curry leaves, onion pieces, red chilli powder, salt and cabbage with water as necessary and make it into thick paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop 1 tsp full of batter gradually into the oil and fry the contents till they turn into golden brown.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot, as they would be crispy.

title: Cauliflower Pakodi
subtitle: Cauliflower Pakoda
procedure: Separate cauliflower into small flowers and wash them thoroughly.
Add salt to the contents and cook for 5 minutes. As cauliflower takes longer to get fried, cook it before dipping in the besan flour and frying.
Grind ginger and green chillies coarsely.
Add rice flour, red chilli powder, salt, ground ginger and green chilli paste to besan flour and prepare it into thick bajji/pakodi batter by adding water as necessary.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, drop each cauliflower flower dipped in the besan flour batter and fry them till they turn into golden brown.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot.

title: Vegetable Cutlet
subtitle: Vegetable Cutlet
procedure: Wash potatoes thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Cook the contents and peel the skin.
Mash them and keep the contents aside.
Finely chop carrot and cabbage and add green peas to the contents.
Fry green chillies in a deep frying pan by adding 2 tsp oil.
Add the vegetables and salt to the fried contents and sprinkle few drops of water.
Place a lid over the contents; do not add more water.
Once fully cooked, sprinkle garam masala powder on the contents and put off the flame.
Crush dried bread crumbs into fine powder.
Add water to besan flour as necessary and prepare it into smooth paste.
With wet hands, prepare mashed potato contents into lemon-sized balls and spread it out into thin, round vadas using hands.
Stuff the vadas with 1 tsp of vegetable curry and cover it with another similarly prepared mashed potato vada and seal both the vadas around the edges.
Dip the prepared vadas in besan flour batter and press each such prepared vada in dried bread crumb powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry each cutlet till it turns into golden brown and serve.
note: It tastes better when consumed with tomato sauce.

title: Ullipayi Chakralu
subtitle: Onion Rings
procedure: Peel onions and cut them into round, thin rings.
Separate each ring without breaking them.
Add corn flour, maida flour, salt and red chilli powder together and by adding water as necessary, prepare it into smooth batter similar to preparing bajjis/pakodis.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, dip each onion ring in the prepared batter and drop in the oil and fry them till they turn into golden brown.
Fry the entire content in the same manner and serve.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot with tomato sauce.

title: Bread Bonda
subtitle: Bread Bonda

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Cook potatoes and peel their skin.
Mash the contents into smooth paste by using hands.
Finely chop onions and green chillies.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 4 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, mustard seeds and split chana dal.
Add onions, green chillies and curry leaves to the contents and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add mashed potato and salt to the fried content and mix well.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Prepare lemon-sized balls of the contents and keep them aside.
Dip bread slices in water and press each of them in between the palms and drain water from it.
Place the prepared potato curry balls in the bread and seal it on all sides.
Prepare the entire contents in the same manner.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, deep fry the prepared contents.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot with tomato sauce.

title: Chuduva Mixture
subtitle: Snack With Flaky Rice

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Soak split chana dal in water for 2 hours.
Drain water completely from the contents and dry on a dry-cloth for 1 hour.
Sauté/roast peanuts in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, clean the chaff of the peanuts and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal till it turns into golden brown.
Transfer the contents into a wide plate.
Sauté flaky rice in the deep frying pan without oil on low flame.
Once fried, add fried flaky rice to the fried split chana dal and mix the contents well.
In the same pan, add 2 tsp oil and fry the remaining flaky rice contents and fry.
Add curry leaves to the contents and fry.
Add the contents to the fried split chana dal.
Add the fried peanuts, salt and red chilli powder to the contents and store in a dry container.
Place a lid tightly over the contents.
note: It stays fresh for up to 1 month. Use only cooking oil and avoid using previously used oil.

title: Boodidagummadi Garelu
subtitle: Ash Gourd Vadas
procedure: Peel ash gourd and cut it into small pieces. Grating or grinding the ash gourd in a food processor/mixie also works very well.
Add salt to the cut pieces and tie them tightly in a cloth and set aside for 4–5 hours. This drains the water completely from the pieces.
Soak urad dal in water for 4–5 hours.
Drain water completely and grind urad dal into paste. Add water slowly and as required while grinding. The paste should be thick.
Add salt to the paste.
Finely chop onions and green chillies and add them to the paste and mix well.
Add ash gourd pieces and cumin seeds to the paste and mix well.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan. Once heated, prepare vadas from the paste, put in oil, and fry till golden brown.
note: This should be consumed hot.

title: Cabbage Garelu
subtitle: Cabbage Vadas
procedure: Soak urad dal in water for 4 to 5 hours.
Drain water completely and grind the soaked urad dal into smooth paste similar to preparing vadas without adding water.
Add salt to the smooth paste.
Finely chop cabbage leaves, green chillies, and onions and add them to the smooth paste.
Place a thick bottomed frying pan on a medium flame and pour oil in it.
Take small quantity of paste and gently tap the balls with wet palms to make vadas.
Drop each vada into the heated oil and fry them till they turn golden brown in color.
note: Cabbage vadas go well with coconut chutney or tomato sauce.

title: Aratikaaya Vadalu
subtitle: Green Plantain Vadas
procedure: Peel plantains, cut them into large-size pieces and cook them in water till soft.
Once cooked, completely drain water from it by squeezing them with hands.
Mash the pieces into smooth paste and add besan flour and salt to it.
Finely chop onions and green chillies and mix it well with the prepared plantain and besan paste.
Take small quantities of the prepared paste and mold them in the shape of vadas.
Place a deep frying pan on medium-high flame with oil and heat it.
Once heated, fry vadas in the heated oil till golden brown.
note: These should be served hot.

title: Usiri Pachadi
subtitle: Amla Chutney
procedure: Wash amla thoroughly and dry them with a dry-cloth.
When fully dried, cut them into pieces and remove seeds from them.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into fine powder — no need to add water — and store it in a dry container for 3 days.
On the 3rd day, add salt, turmeric powder and lemon juice to the contents and mix well.
Sun-dry the contents for one full day.
note: Grind seasoning with dried red chillies (about 4), fenugreek seeds (1 tsp), mustard seeds (1 tsp) and asafoetida. Mix the seasoning with 1 cup of chutney and serve. It stays fresh for up to a year when stored in a dry container.

title: Beetroot Pachadi
subtitle: Beetroot Chutney
procedure: Wash beetroot thoroughly, peel it and chop it into small pieces.
Soak tamarind in ½ cup water and prepare puree of it.
Place a thick-bottomed frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, add the chopped beetroot contents and fry till the contents are cooked soft.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and keep the contents aside for cooling.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and mustard seeds in it.
When fried, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind dried red chillies, green chillies, salt, turmeric powder, tamarind puree, garlic cloves and cooked beetroot together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, one spoon of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind.

title: Sorakaya Tokkupachadi
subtitle: Bottle Gourd Chutney

ingredients.name: Bottle gourd
ingredients.quantity: small pieces along with its skin

procedure: Cut bottle gourd along with the skin and its peeled skin into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry green chillies and keep them aside.
Add bottle gourd pieces and salt to the heated oil and place a lid over the contents.
When the skin is fully cooked, put off the flame.
Keep the contents aside and let the contents cool.
Grind tamarind, turmeric powder, garlic, coconut and cooled bottle gourd pieces and skin in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add fried seasoning of mustard seeds, urad dal, curry leaves and dried red chillies to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Cabbage Pachadi
subtitle: Cabbage Chutney
procedure: Finely chop cabbage leaves.
Add salt to cabbage, add 3 tsp oil and fry in a thick bottomed frying pan on a medium flame.
Place a deep lid over the pan and pour some water in the lid in order to cook cabbage soft.
Place a deep frying pan on flame with oil. Roast urad dal, mustard seeds, red chillies and asafoetida or garlic cloves in oil and put off the flame.
Remove cooked cabbage from flame and grind it into smooth paste by adding green chillies, dried red chillies, garlic cloves (if being used), tamarind puree and turmeric powder.
Pour roasted seasoning over the prepared chutney, mix well, and serve.

title: Capsicum Pachadi
subtitle: Capsicum Chutney
procedure: Wash capsicum thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry green chillies, dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and when fried, keep the contents aside.
Add the remaining oil to the frying pan and when heated, add the capsicum pieces and place a lid over the contents.
Place a lid over the contents and stir the contents frequently on low flame.
When the contents are fully cooked, put off the flame.
Add tamarind puree, salt, turmeric powder, garlic cloves and dried red chillies to the contents and mix well.
Garnish with the fried urad dal, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Bacchali Koora Pachadi
subtitle: Chinese Spinach Chutney
procedure: Thoroughly wash Chinese spinach leaves and finely chop them.
Place a thick bottomed frying pan and roast urad dal, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and keep them aside.
In the same pan, add finely chopped Chinese spinach leaves and fry it on low flame.
Once fried, remove from flame.
Mix fried Chinese spinach leaves, salt, turmeric powder, tamarind, peeled garlic cloves and dried red chillies and grind the contents coarsely in a food processor/grinder/mixie.
Add the roasted urad dal, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds to the prepared chutney and mix well.
note: This resembles chutney made of sorrel gongura leaves. Once fried, Chinese spinach leaves will lose their stickiness.

title: Kobbari Mamidikaya Pachadi
subtitle: Coconut And Raw Mango Chutney
procedure: Cut coconut and raw mango into small pieces and keep aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
When fried, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind dried red chillies, turmeric powder, salt, coconut and raw mango pieces together into a smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Karivepaku Pachadi
subtitle: Curry Leaf Chutney
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, dried red chillies and asafoetida.
Add curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry for another 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind tamarind, salt, turmeric powder, jaggery and fried seasoning including curry leaves into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind. It goes well with Idlies, Dosas and Rice.

title: Kottimeera Pachadi
subtitle: Coriander Leaves Chutney
procedure: Clean coriander of stalks.
Grind coriander leaves, tamarind puree, green chillies, salt, turmeric powder and jaggery in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
note: It goes well with rice and Idlis.

title: Vankaya Banda Pachadi
subtitle: Eggplant Chutney
procedure: Apply oil to the outer skin of the eggplants, directly place them whole on low flame and roast.
Once completely roasted — the eggplant will turn soft — put off the flame.
Peel the skin of eggplants and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the dried red chillies for three minutes.
When cooled, grind green chillies, dried red chillies, coriander leaves, turmeric powder and salt in a food processor/mixie coarsely.
Add the eggplant contents and tamarind puree to the ground contents and grind them into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add the fried contents to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Vankaya Igurupachadi
subtitle: Eggplant Chutney
procedure: Apply oil to the outer skin of the eggplants, directly place them whole on low flame and roast.
Once roasted on all sides, put off the flame.
Wash them with cool water. Peel the skin of eggplants and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 1 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and urad dal and then put off the flame.
Grind green chillies, dried red chillies, coriander leaves, fried eggplants, turmeric powder and salt in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal and add it on the prepared chutney.

title: Mentikoora Pachadi
subtitle: Fenugreek Leaf Chutney
procedure: Chop fenugreek leaves after separating leaves from stems.
Wash the chopped leaves thoroughly.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and fry the chopped leaves in 4 tsp oil till the contents are cooked soft.
When cooked, keep the contents aside for cooling.
Place the frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind fenugreek leaves, dried red chillies, green chillies, tamarind, turmeric powder and salt together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding a small amount of water if necessary.
Add the fried seasoning to the ground chutney and serve.
note: As per taste, add garlic cloves to the contents of the chutney while grinding.

title: Vellulli Karam
subtitle: Garlic Chutney
procedure: Peel the garlic and set the cloves aside.
Boil ½ glass of water and soak tamarind in it.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies.
Add urad dal to the contents and fry for 2 minutes.
Grind dried red chillies, urad dal, turmeric powder and salt in a food processor/mixie.
Add garlic cloves and tamarind to the ground contents and grind the whole contents into smooth paste.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 100 gm of tamarind paste. It remains fresh for up to one month when refrigerated.

title: Allam Pachadi
subtitle: Ginger Chutney
procedure: Soak tamarind in water and prepare thick puree of it.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds till it crackles.
Add red chilli powder and mix for 15 seconds. Add tamarind puree to the fried mustard seeds and cook for 2 or 3 minutes.
Put off the flame and add salt and turmeric powder to the contents.
Wash ginger thoroughly and dry it with a dry-cloth.
Peel the skin of it and chop it into 1-inch small pieces.
Grind ginger pieces and jaggery together into smooth paste.
Add the ground paste to the prepared tamarind puree. Mix the contents well and serve.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, 50 gm of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind. It goes well with Idlies, Dosa and Vadas. It can be stored for 2 to 3 months under refrigeration.

title: Mamidi Allam Pachadi
subtitle: Mango-Ginger Chutney
procedure: Wash ginger-mango thoroughly and peel its skin.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind tamarind puree, ginger-mango, salt, turmeric powder and fried red chillies in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: It goes well with idlis, dosas and rice.

title: Aritikaya Pachadi
subtitle: Green Plantain Chutney

ingredients.name: Seasoning: Split yellow chick pea flour

procedure: Cut plantains into large-size pieces along with its skin.
Cook these pieces by adding water. Plantains can also be roasted directly on flame similar to eggplants.
When cooked, peel off the skin and mash it using hands or mortar.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry split Yellow Chick Pea Flour, urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add slit green chillies, red dried chillies and curry leaves and fry for another 2 minutes.
Add salt and mashed plantain to the fried seasoning and mix well.
note: This is a traditional dish ideal for those who are recovering from illness.

title: Chintakaya Pachadi
subtitle: Green Tamarind Chutney
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies.
Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida and fry for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame.
Wash tamarind thoroughly and hand grind it in a mortar to remove any seeds.
Mix tamarind with salt and turmeric powder in a food processor/mixie for a minute.
Add dried red chillies to the contents and grind the contents by adding water as necessary — do not add more water.
Add fried seasoning to the ground chutney and serve.

title: Paccimirapa Pachadi
subtitle: Green Bell Pepper Chutney
procedure: Wash green/bell peppers thoroughly and nip off their pedicels. Slit the peppers along their length.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add green pepper pieces and fry the contents frequently.
When fully fried, put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame.
Grind fried green peppers, salt, turmeric powder, tamarind puree and fried seasoning into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, 2 tsp of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind.

title: Idli Pachadi
subtitle: Idli Chutney

ingredients.name: Split chana dal / yellow chickpea flour

procedure: Soak split chana dal in water for 2 hours.
Cut coconut into small pieces.
Completely drain water from the soaked chana dal.
Grind chana dal, coconut, salt, tamarind puree, green chillies and fried dried red chillies into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding a small amount water if necessary.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, mustard seeds and asafoetida.
Add curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry for another 1 minute.
Put off the flame and add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind. It goes well with dosas, vadas and idlies.

title: Dosakaya Pachadi
subtitle: Yellow Cucumber Chutney
procedure: Peel cucumber and check for its bitterness. Do not use if bitter.
Cut it into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried red chillies and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind dried red chillies, green chillies, turmeric powder, tamarind puree and salt in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add cucumber pieces to the ground contents and coarse grind it for 10 seconds.
Add fried mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida to the ground chutney and mix the contents well.
note: This preparation goes well with rice.

title: Mamidikaya Pachadi
subtitle: Mango Chutney
procedure: Peel mangoes and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind mangoes, dried red chillies, salt and turmeric powder in a food processor/mixie into smooth/semi-coarse paste.
Add the remaining seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Mamidikaya Teepi Pachadi
subtitle: Mango Sweet Chutney
procedure: Cut mangoes into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies.
Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida and fry the contents.
Grind mango pieces, salt, turmeric powder, fried red chillies and jaggery in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the remaining fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Pesarapappu Pachadi
subtitle: Mung Bean Chutney

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Soak moong dal in water for 4 hours.
Completely drain water from the soaked dal.
Add dried red chillies, asafoetida and salt to the mung bean and grind them together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
note: Preparation of this dish is very easy. This dish tastes best when consumed with hot rice and ghee. If a slightly sour taste is preferred, lemon juice can be added to the chutney. Garlic should not be used with this chutney.

title: Pesarapappu Mamidikaya Pachadi
subtitle: Mung Bean And Raw Mango Chutney

ingredients.name: Moong dal / mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Soak mung bean in water for 4 hours.
Cut mango into small pieces and keep it aside.
Completely drain water from the soaked moong dal.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame by adding oil.
When oil is heated, fry/roast dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
When fried, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind soaked moong dal, mango pieces, dried red chillies and salt together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Add fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Ullikaram
subtitle: Onion Chutney
procedure: Peel onions and wash them thoroughly.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add onions and fry till they turn into golden brown.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, grind onions, salt, turmeric powder and tamarind into a coarse paste in a food processor/mixie/grinder.
note: If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of it may be used. The chutney should be coarse ground.

title: Pachi Vellakaya Pachadi
subtitle: Raw Wood Apple Chutney
procedure: Break wood apple and take out the contents into a vessel.
Add 1 cup of water to the contents and cook it on low/medium flame.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and keep the contents aside to cool.
Grate coconut and keep it aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Grind fried red chillies, green chillies and salt in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Add grated coconut and cooked wood apple contents to the ground paste and grind the whole contents into smooth paste.
Add curd/yogurt and turmeric powder to the contents.
Garnish the chutney with finely chopped coriander.
Add fried mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds to the contents and serve.

title: Maagaya Pachadi
subtitle: Raw Mango Pickle Chutney
procedure: Grind green chillies and coriander leaves in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add Maagaya pickle to the contents and grind it into smooth paste.
Add ½ cup of curd/yogurt to the contents and mix well.
note: It goes well with Idlies, Dosas and Rice. (Maagaya: see recipe for Raw Mango Pickle)

title: Tokku Pachadi
subtitle: Raw Mango Chutney
procedure: Wash mangoes thoroughly.
Dry mangoes with a dry cloth and peel them.
Cut mangoes into small pieces and sun-dry them for 4 hours.
Grind mango pieces along with salt and turmeric powder in a food processor/mixie for one round.
Store the contents in a dry container for 3 days and place a lid over the contents.
Replace the contents on the 3rd day into a wide plate.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds on low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind fenugreek seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Peel garlic cloves and clean them.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, put off the flame.
Add garlic cloves and red chilli powder to the semi-cooled oil.
When oil is cooled, add it to the ground mango chutney along with fenugreek powder and mix the contents well.
Store it in a dry container.

title: Beerapottu Pachadi
subtitle: Ridge Gourd Skin Chutney
procedure: Wash ridge gourd thoroughly and cut it into small pieces along with its skin.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and mustard seeds.
When fried, put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, add ridge gourd pieces and salt and place a lid over the contents.
Reduce flame and stir the contents from time-to-time.
Pour ½ glass of water over the lid to cook the contents well with minimal amount of oil.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame.
Add tamarind puree, coconut, garlic cloves, green chillies, turmeric powder and fried seasoning to the cooked contents.
Grind all the contents together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste. Do not add water to the contents while grinding them into chutney.

title: Perugu Nuvvulapachadi
subtitle: Sesame Seeds Chutney
procedure: Grind sesame seeds and green chillies together into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Add the ground paste to the curd/yogurt. Add salt and two tsp of lemon juice to it.
Mix the contents well and keep it aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, curry leaves and green chilli pieces.
Once fried, put off the flame and add the fried seasoning to the curd/yogurt.
Mix the contents well and serve.
note: This goes well with idlies, rice or vadas.

title: Nuvvula Pappu Teepi Pachadi
subtitle: Sesame Seed Sweet Chutney
procedure: Sauté/roast sesame seeds in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without oil.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, grind the seeds into fine powder in a food processor/mixie.
Add the powder to the tamarind puree and mix well.
Add jaggery, salt and turmeric powder and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds in it.
Add red chilli powder to the fried seasoning and fry for 15 seconds. Put off the flame.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste may be used. It goes well with Vadas and Idlies.

title: Gongoora Pachadi
subtitle: Sorrel Leaves Chutney
procedure: Wash sorrel leaves thoroughly by removing stalks.
Dry the leaves on a dry cloth.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies and keep the contents aside.
Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds to the contents and fry for 1 minute.
Add the remaining oil to the contents and add sorrel leaves.
Place a lid over the contents and reduce the flame.
Stir the contents from time-to-time and fry the contents well.
Once fried, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Peel garlic cloves and keep them aside.
Grind fried red chillies and salt in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Add sorrel leaves and garlic cloves to the contents and grind for 1 round.
Add fried mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds to the contents and serve.
note: Do not add water to the contents. If it is not possible to grind in a food processor/mixie, use mortar to mix the contents.

title: Chilagadadumpa Paccadi
subtitle: Sweet Potato Chutney
procedure: Wash sweet potatoes thoroughly and cut them into small 1-inch pieces.
Soak tamarind in water and keep aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds and asafoetida in it.
Add curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry for another 1 minute.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Grind sweet potato pieces, turmeric powder, soaked tamarind, salt, green chillies and fried dried red chillies into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: This chutney resembles 'kobbari paccadi' coconut chutney. If tamarind is not available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste can be used.

title: Chintachiguru Pachadi
subtitle: Tender Tamarind Leaves Chutney
procedure: Squeeze tender shoots of tamarind tree to remove the stalks from them.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp of oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies.
Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida and fry for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add the tender shoots of tamarind tree and reduce the flame.
Place a lid over the contents and stir the contents frequently.
When the contents are fully steam-cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the shoots along with salt, turmeric powder, green chillies and fried red chillies in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and serve.

title: Tamata Teepi Pachadi
subtitle: Tomatoes Sweet Chutney
procedure: Peel onions, wash them thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Cut green chillies into small pieces.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add onions and green chillies and reduce the flame. Fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add tomatoes, turmeric powder, salt and ½ glass of water.
Place a lid over the contents and cook well.
When fully cooked, add sugar to the contents.
Mix besan flour in ½ cup of water and add it to the cooking contents.
Cook the contents for 2 minutes and put off the flame.
note: This goes well with rice and chapattis. Children generally like to eat this due to its sweet taste.

title: Kandipachadi
subtitle: Toor Dal Chutney
procedure: Sauté/roast toor dal in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without oil.
Once roasted, keep the contents aside for cooling.
Place another deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and urad dal and put off the flame.
Grind roasted toor dal, coconut, salt, fried dried red chillies, cumin seeds and garlic cloves into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding a small amount water.
Add fried seasoning to the prepared chutney and mix well.
note: The dish goes well with 'ullipaaya pulusu'. Garlic can be used as per taste and ground along with other ingredients in step 5.

title: Tamata Pachadi
subtitle: Tomato Chutney
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds and dried red chillies and keep the contents aside.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Add tomatoes to the same frying pan and place a lid over the contents.
Reduce the flame and let the contents cook.
Peel garlic cloves and keep aside.
When tomatoes are cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind cooked tomatoes, garlic, salt, turmeric powder, tamarind puree, coriander seeds, dried red chillies and green chillies in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and add them to the chutney and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Velagapandu Pachadi
