subtitle: Ripe Wood Apple Chutney
procedure: Break wood apples and remove the shells.
Take the contents of the wood apple separately.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Grind green chillies, salt and fried red chillies in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add wood apple cream and jaggery powder to the ground paste and grind it in a mortar — no need to add water.
Add the fried seasoning to the ground chutney and serve.
note: This chutney cannot be prepared in a food processor/mixie and it should only be prepared using a mortar. It stays fresh for 5–6 months.

title: Nimmakaya Ooragaya
subtitle: Lemon Pickle
procedure: Soak lemon in lukewarm water for 1 hour and then dry them with a dry-cloth.
When fully dried, cut them into pieces.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the contents and store it in a dry container for 3 days.
On the 3rd day, squeeze lemon pieces and separate juice from the pieces.
Sun-dry the contents separately; if on a hot day, 4 hours would be sufficient for drying.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds on low/medium flame and put off the flame.
Once cooled, grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add asafoetida and put off the flame.
Once semi-cooled, add red chilli powder and let the contents fully cool.
Add lemon pieces, juice and fenugreek powder to the contents and mix them well.
Store the contents in a dry container.
note: Use dry spoons or ladles while using the pickle. If lemon is not juicy, use fewer lemon pieces in the juice.

title: Nuvvula Pachadi
subtitle: Sesame Seed Chutney
procedure: Sauté/roast sesame seeds in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without oil.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, grind the seeds into fine powder in a food processor/mixie.
Add the powder to the tamarind puree and mix well.
Add salt and turmeric powder and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds in it.
Add red chilli powder to the fried seasoning and fry for 15 seconds. Put off the flame.
Add the fried seasoning and curry leaves to the prepared chutney and serve.
note: It goes well with Vadas and Idlies. Jaggery may be added for a sweet variant.

title: Mamidi Pindela Menti Mukkalu
subtitle: Pickle With Raw Tender Mangoes
procedure: Add tender mangoes to water and wash them thoroughly.
Dry them using a dry cloth and cut them into small pieces by removing their kernels.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies.
Now add mustard seeds, asafoetida and fenugreek seeds and fry for 2 more minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried contents along with salt in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Add this fine powder, turmeric and oil to the cut mango pieces and mix the contents well.
note: The pickle should be used the day next to its preparation. The pickle tastes better due to its sour and astringent taste.

title: Mamidi Allam Mukkalu
subtitle: Spiced Mango-Ginger Pieces
procedure: Wash ginger-mango thoroughly and peel their skin.
Cut them into ½-inch small pieces and keep them aside.
Cut green chillies into ½-inch pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry red chilli powder and asafoetida.
Add the fried content to the ginger-mango pieces.
Add salt and lemon juice to the contents and mix the contents well.
note: The dish should be served the next day to the preparation. It goes well with thickened dal mudda pappu and rice.

title: Dosakaya Avakaya
subtitle: Indian Cucumber Pickle
procedure: Wash cucumbers and dry them with a dry-cloth.
Cut dried cucumbers into small pieces along with its skin.
Check for its bitterness; use only if not bitter.
Take a deep-bottomed vessel and add mustard powder, salt and red chilli powder.
Mix the contents well and add oil to it.
Add cucumber pieces to the mixed contents along with turmeric powder and asafoetida.
Mix the contents well and store it in a dry container.
note: Use a dry spoon for serving the pickle. Sesame seed oil is best for this pickle though other cooking oil can also be used. To make mustard powder, grind mustard seeds in a mixie/grinder.

title: Mentikaya
subtitle: Raw Mango Pickle With Fenugreek Powder
procedure: Wash mangoes thoroughly and dry them with a dry-cloth.
Cut mangoes into small pieces along with their skin with their stones.
Remove the kernel and clean the pieces.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds on low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, grind fenugreek seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, put off the flame and let the oil semi-cool.
Add red chilli powder and asafoetida and let the contents cool.
Add the cooled contents to the mango pieces.
Add salt, turmeric powder and fenugreek powder to the contents and mix well.
Store it in a dry container.
note: Tie either a dry cloth or a plastic cover around the lid tightly to prevent drying in summer and forming fungus during rainy season. This method is known as "vasini kattu".

title: Maagaya
subtitle: Raw Mango Pickle
procedure: Wash mangoes thoroughly with water and peel them.
Cut mangoes into thin, long pieces.
Add salt and turmeric powder and store in a dry container for 3 days.
On the 3rd day, squeeze the contents hard using hands and separate pieces from juice.
Sun-dry the mango pieces and the juice separately in various trays.
One day of drying would be sufficient for the juice; more than one day would dry up the juice. Plan to prepare the pickle in peak summer so that one day of sun-drying the juice would be sufficient.
Sun-dry the pieces for 2 days.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds on low/medium flame and then put off the flame.
Once cooled, grind fenugreek seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, put off the flame.
When oil is semi-cooled, add red chilli powder and asafoetida and let the contents cool.
Add the contents to the mango juice.
Add mango pieces to the mango juice and mix the contents well.
Store the contents in a dry container.
note: As required, take a small quantity of the pickle in a bowl using a dry spoon and serve. You can make chutney with this pickle to go with idlis, dosas and rice. Grind green chillies about 4 and coriander leaves 1 bunch in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste. Add maagaya pickle about 5 tbsp to the contents and grind it into smooth paste. Add ½ cup of curd/yogurt to the contents and mix well.

title: Usirikaya Ooragaya
subtitle: Amla Pickle
procedure: Wash amla thoroughly and then dry them with a dry-cloth.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add half the quantity of oil to it.
When oil is heated, add fully dried amla to it and place a lid over the contents.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When the contents are fully cooked, put off the flame and let them cool.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds on a low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind fenugreek seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, add asafoetida and put off the flame.
When the contents are semi-cooled, add red chilli powder and let the contents fully cool.
Add amla, salt, turmeric powder and fenugreek powder to the contents and mix them well.
Store the contents in a dry container.
note: It remains fresh for 4-5 months when stored in a dry container.

title: Tamata Niluva Pachadi
subtitle: Tomato Pickle
procedure: Wash tomatoes thoroughly and dry them using a dry-cloth.
When fully dried, cut them into pieces.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the contents, place a lid tightly over a dry container and store the contents over-night.
Next day, squeeze the contents tightly using hands and separate juice from pieces.
Add tamarind to the extracted juice.
Sun dry tomato juice and pieces separately for 3 days.
On the 3rd day, grind tomato pieces in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Squeeze tamarind and remove seeds from the content.
Add the ground tomato paste to the tomato juice and sun-dry the contents till the entire juice evaporates.
Peel garlic and clean them.
Sauté/roast fenugreek seeds in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind roasted fenugreek seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, put off the flame and add mustard seeds and garlic cloves (optional).
Add red chilli powder to the fried contents and add the contents to the prepared chutney.
To add asafoetida, do not use if you have added garlic; fry it in heated oil and mix it with the contents.
note: It stays fresh for up to 1 year when stored in a dry container with tight lid. Add salt, tamarind and red chilli powder as per taste but the method of preparation would remain the same.

title: Aavakaya Ooragaya
subtitle: Raw Mango Pickle
procedure: Sun-dry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds separately.
When fully dried, grind mustard seeds in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Sun-dry salt and grind it in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Wash mangoes thoroughly and dry them with a dry-cloth.
In a wide and deep vessel, add mustard seed powder, red chilli powder and salt in equal quantities and mix them together.
Add mango pieces to the mixed contents. For 1 bowl of mixed masala powder, add 1½ bowls of mango pieces.
Add fenugreek seeds, asafoetida and oil to the contents and mix the contents well.
Store the contents in a dry container for 3 days and tightly place a lid over the contents.

On the 3rd day, mix the entire contents either with a very dry spoon or with dry hands well from the bottom of the container and replace the lid tightly over the contents. This way, the contents remain fresh without getting spoiled.
note: See to it that after mixing the contents on the 3rd day, oil is floating above the mango pieces. Immediately after preparing mustard seed powder, add salt to the contents to prevent it from turning bitter. Instead of asafoetida, garlic can be used.

title: Chitti Vadiyalu
subtitle: Small Crisp Condiments With Urad Dal
procedure: Soak urad dal the previous night in water.
Next morning, wash urad dal thoroughly and grind it in a food processor/wet grinder by adding water as necessary; do not use mixie, as it may become very hard.
Grind green chillies, salt and asafoetida in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste and add the contents to the batter.
Place a tsp full of the prepared batter on a polythene sheet and sun-dry the contents.
The next day, turn the dried contents and dry them fully and store in a dry container.
note: It stays fresh for up to a year if stored in a dry container. It goes well with "sambar"; fry them in heated oil.

title: Minapa Pottu Vadiyalu
subtitle: Crisp Condiments With Black Gram Chaff
procedure: Soak urad dal for 5 hours.
Grind urad dal in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add chaff, salt, green chillies and asafoetida to the contents and grind them in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste (not smooth) by adding water as necessary.
Place a tsp full of ground paste on a polythene bag (e.g. a Ziploc bag) and dry them in the sun. On the second day, turn the vadiyalu on the other side and allow them to dry in the sun.
note: When fried in heated oil, they become crispy. It goes well with rice and ghee when consumed hot.

title: Oora Mirapakayalu
subtitle: Buttermilk Soaked Green Chillies
procedure: Wash green chillies thoroughly and poke each one with a fork.
Add turmeric powder, salt and ajwain to sour buttermilk and add green chillies to it.
Keep the contents aside for 3 days.
On the 3rd day, squeeze green chillies and sun-dry them.
On the same evening, add the dried chillies to the left-over buttermilk.
Repeat the process till the entire buttermilk is dried up.
When the contents are fully dried under the sun, store the contents in a dry container.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour. Fry the contents as necessary in heated oil and eat it along with dal to taste better. Thin green chillies are very spicy; use them as per taste.

title: Ullivadiyalu
subtitle: Crisp Condiments With Onions

ingredients.name: Black gram urad dal with chaff

procedure: Wash urad dal thoroughly and soak it overnight.
Next morning, wash urad dal thoroughly till it is cleaned off its chaff; if you wish to prepare Pottuvadiyalu, let this chaff remain in a strainer.
Chop onions into small pieces.
Grind green chillies and salt in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Grind urad dal in a food processor/wet grinder by adding water as necessary; do not use mixie, as it may become very hard to grind.
Add onions and green chilli paste to the ground urad dal paste and mix well.
Place a tsp full of the prepared Vadiyalu on a polythene sheet and sun-dry the contents for 4-5 days.
note: It stays fresh for up to a year if stored in a dry container. Finely chopped cabbage can also be added to the ground paste as per taste. One can also prepare 'chittivadiyalu' without adding onions and cabbage to the ground paste. These are also known as 'minapavadiyalu'.

title: Saggubiyyam Vadiyalu
subtitle: Crisp Condiments With Sago
procedure: Soak sago in water for 30 minutes.
Cook sago in 4 cups of water on low/medium flame, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Grind green chillies and cumin seeds into coarse paste and add to the cooked sago along with salt.
Mix well and allow the contents to cool.
Place a tsp full of the prepared batter on a polythene sheet and sun-dry the contents.
The next day, turn the dried vadiyalu and dry them fully on the other side.
Store in a dry container once fully dried.
note: When fried in heated oil, they become crispy. Best served as a side dish with rice and dal. Note: Method partially inferred from PDF layout; some content was cut off at page boundary.

title: Gummadikaya Koora
subtitle: Pumpkin Curry
procedure: Peel and cut pumpkin into small cubes.
Soak split chana dal for 30 minutes and drain.
Cook pumpkin and chana dal together with salt and turmeric in a pan on low/medium flame with a lid until tender.
Add grated jaggery to the cooked contents and mix well.
Prepare a seasoning by heating oil and frying mustard seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves, then add to the curry.
Mix well and serve.
note: Method partially inferred from PDF layout; some content was cut off at page boundary. Goes well with rice.

title: Mulagaku Koora
subtitle: Drumstick Leaf Curry
procedure: Clean drumstick leaves of stalks and add water to the contents.
Squeeze leaves with hands and completely drain the water from the contents.
Semi-cook toor dal in a vessel by adding water.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add garlic cloves to the fried content and fry for another 2 minutes.
Add drumstick leaves to the contents and sprinkle some water over the contents.
Add semi-cooked toor dal to the contents and mix well.
Reduce the flame and let the contents cook well.
Stir the contents from time-to-time.
When fully cooked, garnish with grated coconut and put off the flame.
note: Drumstick leaves are a good source of many mineral salts and vitamins. They are very good for health.

title: Boppayi Vepudu
subtitle: Raw Papaya Fry
procedure: Peel papaya and cut it into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add papaya pieces and salt to the contents.
Reduce the flame to low and stir the contents frequently till the contents are cooked well.
Add red chilli powder and cumin seeds and fry for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Bendakaya Vepudu
subtitle: Okra Fry
procedure: Wash okras thoroughly and dry them with a dry cloth.
Cut okras into 1-inch pieces.
Cut onions into small pieces equal to the size of okras.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add okra and onion pieces and fry; do not place a lid over the contents as it may turn sticky.
Reduce the flame and fry continuously.
When fully fried, add salt, cumin seed powder and red chilli powder to the contents and mix well.
note: Fry okras 2-3 hours after cutting them into pieces to avoid stickiness.

title: Bendakaya Koora
subtitle: Okra Curry
procedure: Wash okras thoroughly and dry them with a dry cloth.
Cut okras after 10 minutes into 1-inch pieces; if cut when wet, okras may turn sticky.
Add tamarind puree, salt and turmeric powder to okras and cook them on low/medium flame.
Drain water completely; the water thus drained can be used in Charu or Pulusu.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add the fried content to the cooked okras and put off the flame.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 3 tsp of tamarind paste. It goes well with rice. (*Charu/pulusu: thickened soup)

title: Chikkudukayala Vepudu
subtitle: Beans Fry
procedure: Cut beans into 1-inch pieces by removing excess fiber.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add beans and place a lid over the contents.
Reduce the flame and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
Add salt and stir the contents.
When fully cooked, add cumin seeds and red chilli powder to the contents.
Cook for 1 minute and put off the flame.

title: Mullangi Vepudu
subtitle: Radish And Onion Fry
procedure: Peel radishes and finely chop them.
Peel onions and finely chop them in size similar to radishes.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, add radish and salt to it and place a lid on the pan.
When half-cooked, add onions and fry till the contents are fully cooked.
Once cooked, add red chilli powder and cumin seed powder and fry for another 2 minutes.
note: This tastes best when consumed hot.

title: Dondakaya Vepudu
subtitle: Ivy Gourd Fry
procedure: Wash ivy gourds thoroughly and cut them into thin circles.
Add salt to the cut pieces and squeeze them with hands to drain off water completely from them and keep the contents aside for ½ hour. See note 1.
Chop onions into medium-sized pieces and keep them aside.
Place a thick bottomed frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add ivy gourd pieces and place a lid over the vessel containing the contents.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time and reduce flame to low.
When the contents are half-cooked, add chopped onion pieces and fry the entire contents for another half an hour, stirring frequently.
When ivy gourd pieces are soft, add cumin seeds and red chilli powder to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: The process of adding salt and squeezing away the entire water from ivy gourd pieces makes the pieces to wilt, which would in turn speed-up the process of frying. This dish goes well with rice and chapattis. Ivy gourd is also known as 'gherkins' or 'tindoora'.

title: Beerakaya Vepudu
subtitle: Ridge Gourd Fry
procedure: Peel ridge gourd and cut into small pieces.
Add salt to the contents and mix well.
Drain water completely from the contents by squeezing it with hands.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry ridge gourd pieces in it.
When fully fried, add red chilli powder, salt and cumin seed powder to the fried contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.

title: Capsicum Masala Koora
subtitle: Capsicum Masala Curry
procedure: Wash all the vegetables thoroughly and cut them into 1-inch pieces separately.
Grind onion pieces, ginger, garlic and garam masala powder in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the ground onion paste till it turns into golden brown.
Add capsicum, potato and tomato pieces to the contents and mix well.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the contents and mix well.
Add ½ glass of water to the contents and place a lid over the vessel.
Reduce the flame and cook the contents well.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with chapattis.

title: Capsicum Koora
subtitle: Stuffed Capsicum
procedure: Slit capsicums into 4 pieces each without separating them and keep them aside.
Chop onions into pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add onion pieces and green chillies to the contents and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add salt to the contents and put off the flame. Let the contents cool.
Once cool, grind the fried contents in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add tamarind puree and turmeric powder to the contents and mix well.
Stuff the content in the capsicums.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, add the stuffed capsicums carefully to the oil and place a lid over the contents.
Pour ½ glass of water over the lid and stir the contents frequently.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Mulakkadala Pindikoora
subtitle: Drumsticks And Rice Flour Curry
procedure: Soak rice for 4 hours in water.
Drain water completely and wash rice thoroughly.
Grind soaked rice and coconut in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste by adding ½ glass of water.
Cut drumsticks into 3-inch long pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and urad dal.
Add 3 cups of water to the fried contents and add drumstick pieces to it.
Add salt to the contents and place a lid over the vessel.
When fully cooked, add the ground paste and stir the contents continuously.
See that no lumps are formed.
Add black pepper to the contents.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame.
note: It goes well with sour soup / pulusu. (*pulusu: sour soup)

title: Carrot Beetroot Koora
subtitle: Carrot And Beetroot Curry
procedure: Peel carrot and beetroot and grate them.
Cut green chillies and tomatoes into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the seasoning ingredients.
Add green chillies and semi-fry the contents.
Add grated beetroot, carrot, tomato pieces, salt and turmeric powder to the fried content and place a lid over the vessel.
Reduce the flame and add a small quantity of water to the contents.
When the curry is fully cooked, sprinkle garam masala powder and serve well.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Mulakkadala Ullikaram Koora
subtitle: Drumsticks And Spicy Onion Paste Curry
procedure: Wash drumsticks and cut them into 3–4 inch long pieces.
Peel onions and cut them into pieces.
Place a deep frying pan and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add onions to the contents and semi-fry them.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place the deep frying pan and add the remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, add drumsticks, salt and turmeric powder.
Add ½ glass of water to the contents and place a lid over the contents.
Stir the contents frequently.
When the contents are semi-cooked, add the ground onion paste and tamarind puree to it.
Mix the contents well and place a lid over the contents.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.

title: Aanapakaya Majjigapulusu
subtitle: Buttermilk Soup With Bottle Gourd
procedure: Peel bottle gourd and cut them into 1–2 inch pieces.
Add salt, turmeric powder and 1 glass of water to bottle gourd and cook them.
Grind coconut, coriander seeds and green chillies in a food processor/mixie into smooth pieces.
Add this paste and besan flour to the buttermilk, then add it to the cooked bottle gourd pieces. Cook it for 5 minutes.
Reduce the flame.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add the fried contents to the cooked buttermilk.
Garnish the contents with finely chopped coriander leaves and serve.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour.

title: Bagarabaingan
subtitle: Eggplant/Aubergine Curry
procedure: Slit eggplants into four pieces in such a way that they do not get separated and put them in water.
Place a deep frying pan and add oil to it.
Take the eggplants from the water.
When oil is heated, add eggplants and fry them.
Once fried, take them out, put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Peel onions, wash them and cut them into pieces.
Clean ginger and garlic.
Grind coriander seeds, onions and other masala ingredients along with ginger and garlic in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil used for frying eggplants.
When oil is heated, fry the ground masala in it till it turns into golden brown.
Add tomatoes, salt, turmeric powder to the fried contents.
Add 1 glass of water to it and cook; this is known as gravy.
Once cooked, add the fried eggplants and cook for 5 minutes.
Garnish the contents with finely chopped coriander leaves.
Add bay leaves and serve.

title: Vankaya Kobbari Koora
subtitle: Eggplants/Aubergine And Grated Coconut Curry
procedure: Slit eggplants into 4 pieces in such a way that they do not get separated and put them in water.
Grind salt, green chillies, coconut and sesame seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Take the eggplants out and stuff the ground paste into each eggplant.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry stuffed eggplants, turmeric powder and sprinkle few drops of water.
Place a lid over the contents and reduce the flame.
Stir the contents frequently.
When the contents are semi-cooked, reduce the flame to low/simmer.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: If water is added to the lid placed over the vessel containing eggplant curry, then the contents can be cooked using less oil.

title: Baingan Bhartha
subtitle: Mashed Eggplants/Aubergine Curry
procedure: Apply oil to eggplants and poke them with a knife.
Smoke them on low flame.
Pour cool water on them after smoking and keep them aside.
Finely chop onions, green chillies and coriander leaves.
Cut tomatoes into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add onions and green chillies to the fried content and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add tomatoes to the contents.
Peel the smoked eggplants and mash them into coarse paste in a mortar.
When the tomato masala is fully cooked, add the mashed eggplants to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and add red chilli powder and coriander leaves.
Grind cloves and cinnamon in a food processor/mixie into fine powder and add it to the cooked contents.
Mix the contents well and serve.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Bangaladumpa Koora
subtitle: Potato Curry
procedure: Cook potatoes and peel their skins.
Peel onions and cut them into thin, long pieces.
Cut green chillies into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, mustard seeds and dried red chillies.
Add onions, green chillies and curry leaves to the fried contents and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add 1 glass of water and salt to the contents and cook.
Once cooked, mash potatoes into smooth paste using hands and add it to the contents.
Mix the contents well and cook for 5 minutes.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with Puris and Dosas.

title: Chikkudukaya Teepikoora
subtitle: Beans Sweet Curry
procedure: Remove excessive fiber from beans and cut them into 1-inch pieces.
Wash the pieces thoroughly.
Add tamarind puree, salt, turmeric powder and water as necessary to beans and cook.
Once fully cooked, drain water completely and separate the cooked beans into another vessel.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and urad dal.
Add cooked beans and jaggery powder to the fried contents and mix well.
The curry becomes thin due to the addition of jaggery powder.
Cook till entire water evaporates and then put off the flame.

title: Chikkudukaya Karam Koora
subtitle: Beans Spicy Curry
procedure: Remove excessive fiber from beans and cut them into 1-inch pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies and coriander seeds.
Add split chana dal and urad dal to the semi-fried contents and fry for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried content along with salt into fine powder and keep it aside.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add some more oil to it.
When oil is heated, add beans and turmeric powder along with ½ glass of water to the contents.
Place a lid over the contents and reduce the flame.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When semi-cooked, add tamarind puree to the contents.
Add water as necessary and fully cook the contents.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: As per taste, garnish the curry with grated dried coconut or grated raw coconut.

title: Beans Masala Koora
subtitle: Spicy Curry With Beans
procedure: Peel extra fiber from beans and wash them thoroughly.
Cut them into ½-inch small pieces and keep them aside.
Peel onions and cut them into pieces.
Grind onions and green chillies together in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the seasoning ingredients.
Add the ground onion paste to the fried contents and fry till onion paste turns into golden brown.
Add beans pieces, salt and turmeric powder and mix well.
Place a lid over the vessel and pour ½ glass of water over the lid.
Reduce the flame and stir the contents frequently; see to it that water does not spill into the curry.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.

title: Beans Kobbari Koora
subtitle: Beans With Grated Coconut
procedure: Cut beans and potatoes into ½-inch pieces and add salt to the contents.
Cook the contents well.
Cut onions into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, split yellow chick pea flour and urad dal.
Add onions and curry leaves and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add cooked beans and potato pieces and mix the contents well.
Garnish with grated coconut and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.

title: Potlakaya Kobbari Koora
subtitle: Snake Gourd With Grated Coconut
procedure: Wash snake gourd thoroughly and cut it into small pieces.
Add salt and add ½ glass of water to the contents and cook well. Drain excess water.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add curry leaves to the fried contents and fry for 2 minutes.
Add cooked snake gourd and mix the contents well.
Sprinkle grated coconut over the cooked curry and put off the flame.

title: Potlakaya Vepudu
subtitle: Fried Snake Gourd
procedure: Wash snake gourd thoroughly and cut it into small pieces.
Add salt to the contents and squeeze it using hands to drain water completely.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add snake gourd pieces and fry for 10 minutes.
Cut onions into pieces and add them to the fried contents.
Reduce the flame to low and stir the contents frequently.
Once the contents are fully cooked, add cumin seed powder and red chilli powder to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with chapattis and rice.

title: Pachi Tamatala Koora
subtitle: Raw Tomato Curry
procedure: Peel onions and cut them into small pieces.
Grind onions and green chillies in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal, dried red chillies and mustard seeds.
Add ground onion paste to the fried contents and fry till onion paste turns into golden brown.
Add tomato pieces, salt and turmeric powder to the contents.
Place a lid over the contents; no need to add water, as tomatoes contain water.
Reduce the flame and cook the contents well.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: This goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Tamata Chikkudukaya Koora
subtitle: Tomatoes And Beans Curry
procedure: Cut beans into small pieces and wash them thoroughly.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Grind ginger and green chillies together in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal and mustard seeds.
Add curry leaves and fry for 1 minute.
Add ginger-green chilli paste to the fried content and fry for 1 minute.
Add beans, tomato pieces, turmeric powder and salt to the contents and mix well.
Place a pan over the vessel containing the contents and reduce the flame.
Once cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Cabbage Masala Koora
subtitle: Spicy Cabbage Curry
procedure: Finely chop cabbage leaves and wash them thoroughly and set aside.
Finely chop onions and cut ginger into small pieces.
Add garam masala powder and garlic cloves to the finely chopped onions and ginger. Grind the contents into smooth paste in a food processor/grinder/mixie.
Place a thick bottomed frying pan on flame and pour oil into it.
Once oil is heated, add the prepared onion-garlic-garam masala paste and fry it till it is golden brown in color.
Add the finely chopped cabbage leaves, tomatoes, salt and turmeric powder to the fried garam masala paste and mix well. Add ½ a glass of water to this as it is cooking.
Place a lid over the vessel containing the contents and cook well.
Once cooked, put off the flame.
note: This curry goes well with chapattis/rotis.

title: Kanda Bacchali Koora
subtitle: Yam And Chinese Spinach Curry
procedure: Peel Yam and cut it into small pieces and finely chop the leaves of Chinese spinach. Wash each thoroughly.
Mix the two, add turmeric powder, and cook them together in a pressure cooker for two whistles or until the yam is soft.
Once cooked, completely drain any water from the contents.
Soak tamarind in water and prepare a thick puree of it.
Prepare a smooth paste of mustard seeds by grinding it in a food processor/grinder/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Finely chop ginger and green chillies and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan with 4 tsp oil and heat it.
Once heated, roast split chana dal, urad dal and red dried chilli pieces in it.
Add ginger, green chillies and curry leaves and fry for two minutes.
Add cooked vegetable contents, tamarind puree and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from flame and add smooth paste of mustard seeds and mix well.
note: This is a very traditional Andhra dish.

title: Aviyal
subtitle: Mixed Vegetable Curry With Curd/Yogurt
procedure: Wash all vegetables thoroughly and cut into small pieces.
Add salt to the cut vegetables and cook in a pressure cooker for two whistles by adding ½ glass water to the contents.
Grind coconut and green chillies together into smooth paste and add it to the cooked vegetables.
Cook the contents for another 2 minutes and put off the flame.
Add curd/yoghurt and oil/ghee to the cooked curry and mix well.
note: This goes well with chapattis and rice.

title: Totakoorato Upmakoora
subtitle: Amaranth Leaf Dry Curry

ingredients.name: Split Yellow Chick Pea Flour (for seasoning)

procedure: Finely chop amaranth leaves, wash and drain water completely from it.
Chop ginger and green chillies and split the dried red chillies into halves.
Place a thick bottomed vessel on flame with oil and roast all the seasoning ingredients, except ginger and green chillies in it.
Add ginger and green chillies and fry for 2 minutes.
Add chopped amaranth leaves, salt and turmeric powder to the roasted seasoning and add water.
Place a lid over the vessel and cook by stirring regularly.
Reduce the flame to low.
Once cooked, remove the lid over the vessel and let the contents remain on flame till the entire water is evaporated. Remove from flame.
note: This is a dry curry dish that goes well with rice.

title: Cabbage Avakoora
subtitle: Cabbage Curry With Mustard Paste

ingredients.name: Split Yellow Chick Pea Flour (for seasoning)

procedure: Wash cabbage and finely chop into small pieces.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the chopped cabbage, add half a glass of water to it and cook the contents in a pressure cooker.
Remove from flame after one whistle and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, drain all the water from the contents by squeezing the chopped cabbage.
Place a deep frying pan on flame and add oil.
Roast urad dal, split Yellow Chick Pea Flour, red dried chilli pieces, green chillies, ginger pieces and curry leaves.
Add cooked cabbage leaves and tamarind puree to the seasoning and mix well.
Once mixed thoroughly, put off the flame.
Grind mustard seeds into smooth paste by adding water as necessary in a food processor/grinder/mixie.
Add mustard paste to the contents and mix well.
note: The water in which the cabbage was cooked need not be thrown away. It is nutrient-rich and can be used to make rasam or sambar.

title: Boodidagummadi Pappukoora
subtitle: Ash Gourd And Split Yellow Chick Pea Flour Curry
procedure: Peel ash gourd and cut into 1-inch pieces.

Cook the split chana dal in a thick-bottomed vessel along with 1 cup of water. The chana dal should be soft but still in separate grains, i.e. it should not be overcooked to paste. The dal should also be dry after cooking. If there is excess water, this can be drained and the liquid used for making sambar or rasam.
Cook ash gourd pieces in another vessel by adding salt to the contents.
Once cooked, drain water completely from it.
Place a deep frying pan on low-medium flame and heat 2 tsp oil in it.
Once heated, fry red dried chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add curry leaves and fry for 1 minute.
Add half-cooked split chana dal and cooked ash gourd pieces to the seasoning and mix well.
Garnish the contents with grated coconut and put off the flame.
note: The preparation should be a dry-curry.

title: Aratikaaya Avakoora
subtitle: Green Plantain And Mustard Curry
procedure: Peel plantains and cut large-size pieces into water.
In another vessel transfer the cut plantain pieces and pour water till the pieces are completely covered in the water.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the contents and cook well.
Once the plantain pieces are soft, completely drain water from the contents, mash the cooked pieces and keep it aside.
Add tamarind puree to the mashed plantains.
Grind mustard seeds and asafoetida together into smooth paste by adding a small amount of water.
Cut green chillies, red dried chillies and curry leaves into pieces and keep aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
Once heated, fry/roast urad dal, split chana dal and red dried chillies in it.
Add ginger, green chillies and curry leaves to the seasoning and fry for another 1 minute.
Add mashed plantain along with tamarind puree to the seasoning and mix well.
Cook the contents on low-flame for 5 minutes and then add the ground mustard paste and mix well.
Put off the flame and place a lid over the prepared contents.
note:
1. This is a traditional and typical Andhra "Avakoora" dish.
2. It gets its typical taste due to the mustard seed paste, which adds flavor to the curry.

title: Aratikaaya Upmakoora
subtitle: Green Plantain Dry Curry
procedure: Peel plantains and cut large-size pieces into water.
In another vessel transfer the cut plantain pieces and pour water till the pieces are completely covered in water.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the contents and cook well.
Once the plantains are soft, completely drain water from the contents and mash the cooked pieces and keep it aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and heat oil in it.
Once heated, fry/roast urad dal, split chana dal, mustard seeds and red dried chillies in it.
Add green chillies, curry leaves and ginger pieces to the fried seasoning and fry these for another 1 minute.
Add mashed plantain to the seasoning and mix well.
Add lemon juice and immediately put off the flame.
note: It is important to put off the flame immediately after adding lemon juice; otherwise the flame will turn the contents bitter.

title: Goruchikkudu Nuvvulapappu Koora
subtitle: Cluster Beans And Sesame Powder Curry
procedure: Remove fiber from the cluster beans and cut them into 1-inch small pieces.
Add salt and water as necessary to the beans and cook.
When fully cooked, drain water completely using a strainer.
Sauté/roast sesame seeds on low/medium flame in a deep frying pan.
Transfer the contents into another bowl and let the contents cool.
Grind them in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add curry leaves to the contents and fry for 1 minute.
Add cooked cluster beans to the contents and garnish it with ground sesame seeds.
note: Instead of sesame seed powder, ground coconut can be used for garnishing the curry.

title: Goruchikkudu Teepikoora
subtitle: Cluster Beans Sweet Curry
procedure: Clean cluster beans thoroughly.
Add salt, turmeric powder and ½ glass of water to the beans and cook on low/medium flame.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and urad dal.
Add cooked cluster beans, tamarind puree and jaggery powder and cook till the water from the contents evaporates.

title: Goruchikkudu Avakoora
subtitle: Cluster Beans Curry With Mustard Paste
procedure: Remove fiber from cluster beans and cut them into 1-inch small pieces.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the beans and cook on low/medium flame.
Grind mustard seeds in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, split chana dal and urad dal.
Add green chillies, curry leaves, cooked cluster beans and tamarind puree and mix the contents well.
Reduce the flame and cook for 2 minutes.
Add mustard seed paste to the contents and mix the contents well.
Place a lid over the contents and cook it.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with rice.

title: Bangaladumpa Ullikoora
subtitle: Potato And Onion Curry
procedure: Wash potatoes thoroughly and cut into small pieces.
Cook them in water till they are soft. When cooked, peel their skin.
Peel onions and cut them into small pieces.
Grind onions, green chillies, coriander seeds and garlic cloves in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Place a deep frying pan on flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds and dried red chillies.
Add onion paste and curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry till onion paste turns into golden brown.
Add potato pieces, salt and turmeric powder to the contents.
Gently mix the contents, slightly mash the potatoes, and put off the flame.
note: This goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Bangaladumpa Batani Masalakoora
subtitle: Potato And Green Peas Curry
procedure: Wash potatoes thoroughly and peel them.
Cut them into small pieces.
Peel onions and cut them into small pieces.
Grind onions, ginger, garlic, coriander seeds, cloves and cinnamon in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, reduce the flame to low and fry the ground masala paste.
When fried to golden brown, add potato pieces, tomatoes, peas, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and salt and cook the contents well.
note:
1. This curry goes well with chapattis.
2. Instead of, or in addition to, potatoes, cauliflower can be used as well and the same curry can be prepared.

title: Bangaladumpa Nimmarasam Koora
subtitle: Potato And Lime Juice Curry
procedure: Wash potatoes thoroughly and peel them.
Cut them into pieces and cook them well in water.
Drain water and mash the cooked potatoes and keep it aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal, mustard seeds and dried red chillies.
When fried, add green chillies and curry leaves and fry them for 1 minute.
Add mashed potatoes to the fried contents and mix well. Remove from flame.
Add lime juice, turmeric powder and salt to the curry and mix the contents well.

title: Kakarakaya Masala Koora
subtitle: Bitter Gourd Masala Curry
procedure: Select short-sized bitter gourd and wash them thoroughly.
Slit them into four pieces without separating them.
Remove seeds from the bitter gourd.
Add tamarind, salt and turmeric powder to the pieces and cook them by adding ½ cup water.
Once cooked, drain water completely from the contents.
Chop onions into small pieces and grind it along with garlic, cinnamon, cloves and ginger in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add red chilli powder to the ground contents and stuff the cooked bitter gourds with the contents.
Tie the stuffed bitter gourds with a thread.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.

When oil is heated, gently fry the stuffed bitter gourds — see to it that the slit pieces do not get separated. One way to ensure this is to shake the contents of the entire pan without stirring them.
Deep fry the contents and serve.
note:
1. Do not place lid over the vessel containing the contents.
2. If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Kakarakaya Ullikaram Koora
subtitle: Bitter Gourd And Onion Curry
procedure: Cut bitter gourd into thin, long pieces.
Soak tamarind in water and prepare thin puree of it.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the prepared thin tamarind puree and add it to the bitter gourd pieces and cook the contents on a low/medium flame.
Once cooked, drain water completely from the contents.
Chop onions into small pieces and grind them in a food processor/mixie into coarse paste.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal and mustard seeds.
Add curry leaves and onion paste to the fried content and fry for another 5 minutes.
Add cooked bitter gourd pieces to the contents and stir the contents frequently.
Fry for at least 10 minutes and then sprinkle red chilli powder over the contents.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Kakarakaya Vepudu
subtitle: Bitter Gourd Fry
procedure: Wash bitter gourd thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Add salt to the pieces and squeeze them using hands.
Drain the resulting liquid completely from the contents.
Chop onions into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add bitter gourd pieces and place a lid over the contents.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
Once semi-fried, add onion pieces and stir the contents well.
Reduce the flame and let the contents fry for ½ hour stirring frequently.
Once fried, add red chilli powder and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.

title: Aratikaaya Ullipaya Koora
subtitle: Green Plantain And Onion Curry
procedure: Peel plantains and cut into large-sized pieces. Place in water.
Drain water completely after cutting is completed. Add fresh water till the pieces are completely covered.
Add turmeric powder and salt to the contents and cook well.
Once plantain pieces are soft, drain water completely and mash the pieces using hands.
Chop onions into small pieces.
Grind onions and green chillies coarsely.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds and red dried chillies.
Add curry leaves along with the ground onion paste to the fried seasoning and fry for 5 minutes.
Add mashed plantain to the fried seasoning and mix well.
Add tamarind puree to the contents, mix well and put off the flame.

title: Aratikaya Pakodi
subtitle: Green Plantain And Chickpea Flour Wafers
procedure: Peel plantains and slice into thin and round pieces. Place cut plantain pieces in water.
Prepare batter by mixing besan flour, rice flour, salt, chilli powder and baking powder along with water added as necessary so that it forms a thick paste.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and heat oil.
When heated, dip each plantain slice in besan batter till it is coated completely, and drop into hot oil. At a time, depending on the size of frying pan, about 5-6 pakodas can be fried.
Reduce flame to low and deep fry each "pakodi" till golden brown.

title: Aratidoota Avakoora
subtitle: Banana Stem And Mustard Paste Curry

ingredients.name: Banana stem
ingredients.quantity: 2 pieces about 1 foot long in all

procedure: Cut banana stem into circles. Simultaneously remove the fiber from between the circles by wrapping the fiber around fingers. Discard the fiber.
Chop banana stem circles finely into small pieces — a food processor produces best results.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the pieces of banana stem and mix well.
Squeeze the pieces to completely drain water emanating from them.
Chop green chillies, red dried chillies and ginger into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame along with oil.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, split chana dal, one spoon mustard seeds and red dried chilli pieces.
Add green chillies, curry leaves and ginger pieces to the fried seasoning and fry for a minute.
Add cut pieces of the banana stem, salt, tamarind paste, and turmeric powder to the fried contents and mix well. Sprinkle a small quantity of water on the cooking mixture.
Place a lid over the vessel containing the contents and reduce the flame to low.
Stir the contents frequently.
Prepare smooth mustard paste by grinding it in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
When the pieces of banana stem are cooked well and become soft, add the prepared mustard seed paste to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note:
1. This preparation goes well with rice.
2. The curry should be a dry-curry. Hence, add water in small quantities. Sprinkling of water would be sufficient.

title: Aratipuvvu Avakoora
subtitle: Banana Flower Curry With Mustard
procedure: Nip the pedicels and stalks off the banana flower and wash it thoroughly.
Grind banana flowers coarsely in a food processor/mixie.
Wash the ground flowers in a strainer using water.
Completely drain the water from the ground flowers by squeezing it and keep aside the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal, urad dal, red dried chillies and fenugreek seeds.
Add green chillies and curry leaves to the fried contents and fry for 2 minutes.
Add ground banana flower paste, salt, turmeric powder and tamarind puree to the fried seasoning and mix the contents well.
Sprinkle small quantity of water on the contents and place a lid over the vessel containing the contents.
Reduce the flame to low and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time. This method aids in cooking the contents quickly.
After 5 minutes of cooking, add mustard paste, prepared by grinding mustard seeds into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.

title: Aratikaya Vepudu
subtitle: Green Plantain Fry
procedure: Peel plantains and cut it into small pieces and place in water.
Chop onions into equal size as that of plantain pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan of low/medium flame and add oil.
When oil is heated, remove plantain pieces from water and put in oil along with onion pieces. Add salt and mix the contents well.
Place a lid over the contents and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When plantain pieces are cooked soft, add red chilli powder and cumin seeds powder.
Fry the contents for 2 minutes and put off the flame.
note: This goes well when consumed hot with hot rice and ghee.

title: Chamadumpala Vepudu
subtitle: Colocasia Fry
procedure: Wash colocasia thoroughly and cook them.
Once cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Peel the skins and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry cooked colocasia and stir the contents till they turn into golden brown.
Mix salt, red chilli powder and rice flour together and sprinkle over the fried contents.
Add cumin seeds to the contents.
Add red chilli powder to the contents and mix well.
After 2 minutes, put off the flame and serve.
note: Do not cook colocasia in a pressure cooker, as they become too soft.

title: Kakarakaya Teepikoora
subtitle: Bitter Gourd Sweet Curry
procedure: Wash bitter gourd thoroughly and cut them into thin round pieces.
Soak tamarind in water and prepare puree of it.
Add tamarind puree, salt and turmeric powder to the bitter gourd pieces and cook the contents till bitter gourd is soft.
Once cooked, drain water completely from the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and mustard seeds.
Add bitter gourd pieces and grated jaggery and mix them well. The contents would turn thin once jaggery is added.
Reduce the flame to low and cook the contents till the entire water is evaporated.
note: This goes well with rice.

title: Beerakaya Nuvvulapodikoora
subtitle: Ridge Gourd And Sesame Seed Curry
procedure: Peel ridge gourd and cut it into small pieces.
Add salt to the contents and cook well.
Drain water completely from the cooked contents.
Sauté/roast sesame seeds in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without adding oil to it.
Grind the fried sesame seeds into fine powder in a food processor/mixie.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chilli pieces and urad dal.
Add cooked ridge gourd to the fried seasoning and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add ground sesame seed powder to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: As ridge gourd naturally contains water, there is no need to add water additionally.

title: Beerakaya Vankaya Koora
subtitle: Ridge Gourd And Eggplant Curry
procedure: Cut eggplant into thin long pieces and place them in water.
Peel ridge gourd and cut them into thin, long pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Once cooled, grind the contents into fine powder in a food processor/mixie.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame and add 4 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, remove eggplant pieces from water and put into the oil.
Add ridge gourd pieces, turmeric powder, ground powder and salt to the contents.
Place a lid over the contents and pour ½ glass of water over the lid.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When the contents are semi-cooked, add tamarind puree to it and mix well.
Replace the lid over the contents and let the contents cook well.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note:
1. If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.
2. This dish goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Beerakaya Ullipaya Koora
subtitle: Ridge Gourd And Onion Curry
procedure: Wash ridge gourds thoroughly and peel their skins.
Cut them into thin 3-inch long pieces.
Cut onions into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 3 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add onion pieces to the fried seasoning and fry till they turn into golden brown.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind green chillies, salt and onion pieces into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame and add remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, add ridge gourd pieces and place a lid over the contents.
Reduce flame.
When the contents are semi-cooked, add the ground paste and tamarind puree to the contents and mix well.
Cook the contents for another 5 minutes and put off the flame.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Patholi
subtitle: Dry Chickpea Curry
procedure: Soak split Yellow Chick Pea Flour in water for at least 6 hours.
Drain water completely from it and wash thoroughly.
Grind the soaked Yellow Chick Pea Flour by adding green chillies, dried red chillies, salt and cumin seeds into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie without adding water.
Chop onions into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal and mustard seeds.
When fried, add onions and curry leaves and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add the ground paste to the fried contents and mix them well.
Reduce flame and stir the contents continuously.
The curry would turn into a dry curry after 10 minutes.
note:
1. This curry goes well with rice.
2. The traditional combination is to eat this with "ullipaya pulusu" in the same meal.

title: Guttivankaya Koora
subtitle: Stuffed Eggplant Curry

ingredients.name: Eggplants
ingredients.quantity: ½ kg, small-sized, black and round type

procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp of oil.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, coriander seeds and split Yellow Chick Pea Flour.
After about three minutes, add fenugreek seeds and urad dal and deep fry the whole contents for another two minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried seasoning in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Slit eggplants into 4 pieces without separating them and put them in water. This prevents discoloration of eggplant pieces.
Add salt, turmeric powder and tamarind puree to the powdered contents and mix well.
Remove eggplants from water and stuff the prepared contents in the slit eggplants.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining oil.
When oil is heated, add the stuffed eggplants and place a lid over the contents.
Pour water on the lid — do not add water directly to the curry. The steam produced thereby within the vessel aids in cooking the contents with less usage of oil.
Stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note:
1. If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste.
2. Slit the eggplant carefully so that the pieces do not separate.

title: Sorakaya Kofta
subtitle: Bottle Gourd Kofta
procedure: Peel bottle gourd and grate it. Add salt and ½ glass of water to it and cook well.
Once cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Drain water completely from the contents into another bowl by squeezing it with hands.
In the cooked bottle gourd, mix besan flour and ½ tsp chilli powder and make 1-inch oval shaped balls of it.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, deep fry the prepared balls. Keep the contents aside.
Cut onions into small pieces.
Grind onions, ginger, garlic and garam masala powder in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Wash tomatoes and cut them into pieces. Grind them into smooth paste.
Place the deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the ground onion masala paste till it turns into golden brown.
Add the ground tomato paste to the fried contents and add the drained bottle gourd contents.
Cook the contents for 5 minutes — this is known as gravy.
Add the fried bottle gourd balls to the prepared gravy and mix well.
Garnish the prepared contents with finely chopped coriander leaves.
note: It goes well with rice or chapattis.

title: Dondakaya Kobbari Podikoora
subtitle: Ivy Gourd And Coconut Dry Curry
procedure: Wash ivy gourds thoroughly and cut into ½-inch small pieces cutting each gourd into quarters length-wise and then halves of each piece will give the right size.
Add split chana dal to the cut pieces and add 1 glass of water.
Cook the contents in a pressure cooker for one whistle.
Put off the flame.
Add salt to the contents and completely drain water from the contents.
Place a thick-bottomed frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
When fried, add cooked ivy gourd pieces and split chana dal and mix well.
Garnish the contents with grated coconut and put off the flame after one minute.
note: 1. This dish goes well with rice. 2. Ivy gourd is also known as "gherkins" or "tindoora".

title: Dondakaya Teepi Koora
subtitle: Ivy Gourd Sweet Curry
procedure: Cut ivy gourds into thin long pieces.
Add salt, turmeric powder, tamarind puree, and ½ cup of water to the ivy gourd pieces and cook well in a thick-bottomed vessel on a low/medium flame.
Place a thick-bottomed frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, mustard seeds and dried red chillies.
Add cooked ivy gourd pieces to the fried seasoning and mix the contents well.
Add grated jaggery to the contents and mix well. Mixing of jaggery makes the contents watery.
Put the contents on low flame till the entire water is evaporated and then put off the flame.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind. 2. Due to its sweet taste, children like generally this dish. 3. Ivy gourd is also known as "gherkins" or "tindoora".

title: Dondakaya Ullikaram
subtitle: Ivy Gourd And Onion Curry
procedure: Wash ivy gourds thoroughly and cut them into thin, long pieces.
Peel onions and chop them into pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add onions and green chillies and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Put off the flame.
Put a thick-bottomed frying pan on low/medium flame and add cut ivy gourd pieces, salt and turmeric powder.
Add ½ glass of water to the contents and place a lid over the vessel.
Reduce flame and stir the contents from time-to-time.
Grind the fried seasoning along with onions and green chillies into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
Add the ground paste and tamarind paste to the semi-cooked curry and mix the contents.
When the curry is fully cooked, put off the flame.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of it may be used. 2. This goes well with rice and chapattis. 3. Ivy gourd is also known as "gherkins" or "tindoora".

title: Dondakaya Karam Koora
subtitle: Spicy Ivy Gourd Curry
procedure: Cut ivy gourds into thin, long pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp of oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds, split Yellow Chick Pea Flour and dried red chillies.
When semi-fried, add urad dal and asafoetida and fry the contents.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add ivy gourd pieces and ½ glass of water to the contents.
Place a lid over the contents and reduce the flame. Stir the contents from time-to-time.
Grind the fried seasoning into fine powder including dried coconut or copra in a food processor/mixie.
Add the ground powder to the semi-cooked curry and mix well.
Add salt, turmeric powder and tamarind puree and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of it may be used. 2. This goes well with chapattis. 3. Ivy gourd is also known as "gherkins" or "tindoora".

title: Ullipaya Koora
subtitle: Onion Curry
procedure: Peel onions and chop them into pieces.
Chop green chillies into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, dried red chillies, split Yellow Chick Pea Flour and mustard seeds.
Add onions, green chillies and curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Add 1 glass of water, turmeric powder and tamarind paste to the contents and mix the contents well.
When the curry is fully cooked, add besan flour mixed in water and cook it for another 2 minutes.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of it may be used. 2. This goes well with Puris. 3. This is a good option for those who prefer not eating potato curry with puris.

title: Vankaya Kotimeera Karam Koora
subtitle: Eggplant And Coriander Paste Curry
procedure: Cut eggplants into thin long pieces and put them to water. This prevents discoloration of eggplant pieces.
Drain water completely from the contents.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add eggplant pieces and salt.
Stir the contents and place a lid over the vessel.
Grind coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger and salt into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
When the contents of eggplants are semi-cooked, add the ground paste, turmeric powder and tamarind puree to it and mix well.
Reduce flame and replace the lid over the contents.
Pour water over the lid and steam-cook the contents fully.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Panasakaya Pesarapappukoora
subtitle: Jackfruit and Mung Bean Curry

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Soak moong dal in water for 2 hours.
Drain water completely and wash it thoroughly.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add moong dal and the chopped raw jackfruit to the fried seasoning and add ½ cup of water to the contents.
Place a lid over the vessel and let the contents cook. Reduce the flame.
Once fully cooked — the dal and the jackfruit will be soft — mix asafoetida in ½ tsp water and add it to the contents.
Add salt and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. Raw jackfruit is a somewhat difficult vegetable to work with if starting with whole jackfruit. Chopped raw jackfruit is usually available in most supermarkets and it is best to use this. 2. If starting from the whole jackfruit, the outer spiky skin needs to be shaved off first. Then the jackfruit needs to be cut into small pieces. The central hard core of the jackfruit is discarded. The cut pieces should then be finely chopped in a food processor. During the whole process of cutting the jackfruit, it is important to apply oil liberally to the hands as otherwise the gum of the jackfruit tends to stick to the hands. Finally, the chopped jackfruit should be mixed with oil and turmeric and then stored in the refrigerator for use as necessary.

title: Panasapottu Avakoora
subtitle: Jackfruit And Mustard Curry
procedure: Cook jackfruit pieces with tamarind puree, turmeric powder, salt and sufficient water until soft.
Grind mustard seeds with green chillies and salt into a fine paste.
Add the mustard paste to the cooked jackfruit and mix well.
Prepare seasoning with oil, mustard seeds, dried red chillies, and urad dal.
Add the seasoning to the curry and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 1 tsp of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind puree.

title: Vankaya Chikkudikaya Koora
subtitle: Eggplant And Beans Curry
procedure: Cut eggplants into small pieces and put them to water. This prevents discoloration of eggplant pieces.
Wash beans thoroughly and cut them into 1-inch small pieces.
Remove eggplant pieces from water, and cook eggplant and beans on low/medium flame by adding ½ cup water to the contents till both are soft.
Grind ginger and green chillies into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds and dried red chillies.
Add ginger and green chilles to the fried contents and fry them for another 1 minute.
Add the cooked contents of eggplants and beans to the contents.
Add salt, turmeric powder and tamarind puree to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste. 2. In a similar way, instead of beans, potatoes or plantains can be used for the preparation of the above mentioned curry.

title: Vankaya Ullikaram Koora
subtitle: Eggplant And Onion Curry
procedure: Cut eggplants into thin, long pieces and put them to water. This prevents discoloration of eggplant pieces.
Peel onions and chop them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Once fried, add onions and green chillies to it and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried contents into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
Place a thick-bottomed pan on flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, add eggplant pieces after removing them from the water, salt and turmeric powder to the contents.
Mix the contents well and place a lid over the vessel.
When the contents are semi-cooked, add the ground onion paste and tamarind puree to the contents.
Mix the contents well and replace the lid over the vessel.
Reduce the flame and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
Once fully cooked, put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of tamarind paste. 2. This preparation goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Pullatlu
subtitle: Sour Dosas
procedure: Soak rice and fenugreek seeds in sour buttermilk for 4 hours.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Grind green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add green chilli paste to the ground rice contents and prepare it into thin batter.
Place a flat pan on medium/high flame and apply oil to it.
When heated, spread a ladle full of batter into thin, round dosas and fry.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour.

title: Maidapindi Pullatlu
subtitle: Sour Dosas With All Purpose Flour
procedure: Add maida flour to the sour buttermilk and soak it for 3 hours.
Grind green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the ground contents to the soaked contents and mix well.
Place a flat pan on medium/high flame and apply oil to it.
When heated, spread a ladle full of batter into thin, round dosas and fry both sides.
note: To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour.

title: Atukula Pullatlu
subtitle: Flaky Rice Sour Dosa
procedure: Soak rice and chudva/flaky rice in buttermilk for 4 hours.
Grind the soaked contents in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Grind green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste and add it to the ground rice.
Place a flat pan on medium/high flame and apply oil to it.
When heated, spread a ladle full of batter into thick, round dosas. Fry on both sides and serve.
note: 1. To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour. 2. The dosas would be soft and elastic. 3. Spread batter on pan into thick dosas.

title: Ootappam
subtitle: Pancake with Urad Dal
procedure: Soak urad dal in water for 6 hours.
Wash it thoroughly and grind it in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste by adding water as necessary.
Add Idli ravva and salt to the ground paste and mix the contents well (the batter should be of the consistency that is similar to batter for preparing Idlies).
Keep the batter aside for 8 hours.
Finely chop onions, green chillies and tomatoes.
Place a flat pan on medium/high flame and add 1 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, spread a ladle full of batter on the pan and spread it out into thick dosas (the spread batter should not be thin).
Sprinkle onions, green chillies, tomato pieces and cumin seeds over the pancake and reduce the flame.
Fry both the sides of the pancake till it turns into golden brown and serve.

title: Maida Doselu
subtitle: All Purpose Flour Dosa
procedure: Sieve maida and rice flour together and add salt to the contents.
Add 5 cups of water to the flour and prepare a thin batter and keep it aside for 4 hours.
Place a flat pan on low/medium flame and heat it.
Grease the pan with oil and spread out 1 ladle of batter on the heated pan into round, thin dosas.
Add oil along the circle of the dosa and fry on both the sides.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot with coconut chutney.

title: Minapappu Doselu
subtitle: Black Gram Dosa
procedure: Soak urad dal and rice in water for at least 6 hours.
Wash the soaked contents thoroughly and grind them in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Keep the ground paste aside for at least 4 hours.
Add salt to the contents.
Place a flat pan on low/medium flame and heat it.
Grease it with oil and spread out 1 ladle of batter into thin, round dosas.
Add oil along the circle of the dosa and fry on both the sides and serve.
note: 1. It tastes better when consumed hot with chutney. 2. When these dosas are served with potato curry, they are called Masala Dosas.

title: Kobbari Doselu
subtitle: Coconut Dosa
procedure: Soak rice in water for at least 4 hours.
Wash the soaked rice thoroughly and grind it with coconut pieces in a food processor/mixie into fine paste.
Grind green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the ground green chilli paste to the ground rice and coconut paste and mix the contents well.
The consistency of the batter should be similar to the batter for preparing Dosas.
Place a flat pan on low/medium flame and heat it.
Grease it with ½ tsp oil and spread out 1 ladle of batter into thin, round dosas.
Add oil along the circle of the dosa and fry on both the sides and serve.
note: It tastes better when consumed hot with chutney powder.

title: Pesarattu
subtitle: Green Gram Dosa
procedure: Soak green gram and rice together in water for at least 4 hours.
Wash the contents thoroughly and drain water completely.
Grind the contents along with ginger, green chillies, salt and cumin seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth batter by adding water as necessary.
Finely chop onions into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a flat pan on low/medium flame and heat it.
Grease it with oil and spread out 1 ladle of batter into thin, round dosas. Sprinkle chopped onion on the dosa and press them gently so that they are stuck.
Add oil along the circle of the dosa and fry on both the sides and serve.
note: 1. It tastes better when consumed hot. 2. It goes well even with rice. 3. It is traditionally consumed with upma.

title: Ragula Doselu
subtitle: Finger Millet And Rice Flour Dosa
procedure: Mix rice flour and finger millet flour together and prepare it into smooth batter by adding water as necessary.
Keep the prepared batter aside for 2 hours.
Add salt, cumin seeds and green chillies to the prepared batter and mix well.
Finely chop onions and keep them aside.
Place a flat pan on low/medium flame and heat it.
Grease it with oil and spread out 1 ladle of batter into thin, round dosas.
Sprinkle chopped onion on the dosa and presses them gently so that they are stuck.
Add oil along the circle of the dosa and fry on both the sides and serve.
note: 1. It tastes better when consumed hot. 2. Finger millets are good source for calcium hence are considered healthy. 3. Finger millet dosas tastes similar to Pesarattu.

title: Ada
subtitle: Mixed Lentil Dosa
procedure: Soak rice, moong dal, chana dal and urad dal together in water for 4-5 hours.
Drain water completely and grind the contents in a food processor/mixie by adding salt, green chillies. Add water as necessary.
Place a deep frying pan on medium/high flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, spread a ladle full of batter into thin, round dosas.
Sprinkle onion pieces and cumin seeds over the dosa. Fry on both the sides and serve adding oil as necessary.

title: Nuvvulapodi
subtitle: Sesame Seed Powder

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds White or without skin

procedure: Sauté/roast sesame seeds in a deep frying pan without oil.
Keep the contents aside and let it cool.
Place the deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add ½ tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and asafoetida and keep the contents aside.
Grind the fried sesame seeds, asafoetida, dried red chillies and salt in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Replace the frying pan on low/medium flame and add the remaining oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal and mix it with the ground powder and store the contents.
note: 1. This powder can be preserved for up to one month when stored in a dry container. 2. It goes well with rice.

title: Doselu Podi
subtitle: Dosa Powder
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry split chana dal and dried red chillies for two minutes.
Add urad dal and asafoetida to the semi-fried contents and fry for another 1 minute.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Add salt to the contents and grind the whole contents in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Grind dried coconut or copra into fine powder separately.
Mix both the powders together and store in a container.
note: 1. It goes well with Dosas, Idlies and rice and tastes better when consumed with ghee. 2. Store the contents in a dry container to last long.

title: Vankaya Koora Podi
subtitle: Eggplant Curry Powder
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds, dried red chillies and split yellow chickpea flour till yellow chickpea flour is golden brown.
When semi-fried, add urad dal and fenugreek seeds and fry for another 1 minute.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried seasoning in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
