Grind dried coconut or copra in a food processor/mixie into fine powder separately.
Mix both the powders and add salt to the contents.
Mix the contents and store it in a container.
note: 1. The contents can stay fresh for 2-3 months when stored in a dried container. 2. It can also be used in curries made of eggplants, ridge gourd, coccinia ivy gourd or beans. 3. Add dried coconut copra towards the final stage of preparation to avoid the fried seasoning from getting ground into fine powder.

title: Andhra Charu Podi
subtitle: Andhra Rasam Powder
procedure: Sun-dry all the above mentioned ingredients. Alternately, sauté/roast them in a deep frying pan without oil on low/medium flame.
Grind them in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
While preparing Rasam, add 1 tsp of prepared rasam powder to the water and mix well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 1 tsp ghee to it.
When ghee is heated, fry mustard seeds, dried red chillies and cumin seeds.
Pour the fried contents into the boiling Rasam.
Garnish Rasam with either coriander leaves or curry leaves instead of asafoetida.

title: Mysore Charu Podi
subtitle: Mysore Rasam Powder
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds and dried red chillies.
When semi-fried, add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, cumin seeds and black pepper and fry for another 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried seasoning in a food processor/mixie into fine powder and store it in a dry container.
note: 1. It tastes better when added to Rasam made of Toor dal. 2. It gives a great flavor when cooked with drumsticks and coriander.

title: Kobbaripodi
subtitle: Coconut Powder
procedure: Cut dried coconut into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, and Yellow Chick Pea Flour.
Keep the contents aside and let them cool.
Add coconut pieces, Yellow Chick Pea Flour, garlic cloves, dried red chillies and salt to the fried contents.
Grind the contents in a food processor/mixie into coarse powder.
note: 1. This stays fresh for 2-3 months when stored in a dry container. 2. Instead of garlic, asafoetida can be used.

title: Kandipodi
subtitle: Toor Dal Powder
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and sauté/roast toor dal without adding oil. Stir frequently so that the dal turns a golden brown but not black.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried toor dal in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside to cool.
Grind the fried contents into fine powder and mix it with toor dal powder along with salt.
note: 1. This stays fresh for up to a year if stored in a dry container. 2. Use only fresh cooking oil for this preparation. Avoid reused oil for cooking. 3. Salt and dried red chillies proportions can be changed as per taste.

title: Pesarapodi
subtitle: Mung Bean Powder

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and sauté/roast Mung Bean without adding oil. Stir frequently.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the roasted moong dal in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal, cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside to cool.
Grind the fried contents into fine powder and mix it with Mung Bean powder along with salt.
note: This powder stays fresh for 5-6 months if stored in a dry container.

title: Sambarupodi
subtitle: Sambar Powder
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds and dried red chillies.
When semi-fried, add split chana dal, urad dal, fenugreek seeds and black pepper and fry for 2 minutes.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Cut the dried coconut into small pieces.
Grind the fried contents along with dried coconut in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
Store it in a dry container.
note: This stays fresh for 5-6 months.

title: Karivepaku Karampodi
subtitle: Curry Leaf Powder
procedure: Clean curry leaves and wash them thoroughly.
Spread the wet leaves on a dry cloth and leave over-night to dry.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds and dried red chillies for 2 minutes.
Add urad dal, cumin seeds and asafoetida and fry for another 1 minute.
Add curry leaves and deep fry the contents till curry leaves are crisp and make a crackling sound. Stir frequently.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind the fried contents along with salt, turmeric powder and tamarind in a food processor/mixie into fine powder.
note: 1. If tamarind is not available, use 1 tsp of "Amchur powder". 2. This stays fresh for 5-6 months when stored in a dry container. 3. It goes well with Idlies and Rice and tastes good when consumed with ghee.

title: Pesarapapputo Totakoora Muddakoora
subtitle: Amaranth Leaf And Mung Bean Curry

ingredients.name: Mung Bean green gram dal without skin

procedure: Wash the leaves of amaranth and finely chop them.
Add Mung Bean and half a cup of water to the chopped amaranth leaves.
Cook the contents in a thick-bottomed vessel on a low-medium flame till they become soft.
Add salt to the cooked mixture and put off the flame.
In a deep frying pan, pour oil and roast dried red chillies, urad dal, cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Pour the roasted seasoning on the cooked dal and mix well.
note: 1. The dal should be cooked till thick consistency is obtained. 2. It goes well with rice. 3. To consume dal with chapatti, tomatoes or tamarind puree can also be added while cooking the dal for obtaining thin consistency.

title: Beerapottu Pappu
subtitle: Dal Made Of Ridge Gourd's Skin
procedure: Peel ½ kg ridge gourds.
Grind the skin of the ridge gourds in a food processor/mixie into thick paste and squeeze excess water from the contents.
Semi-cook toor dal on low flame. Cooking in a pressure cooker for one whistle works well. Use just one cup water as the dal should be dry.
Add ground paste and salt to the contents and cook well.
When the contents are fully cooked, put off the flame.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, ½ tsp cumin seeds and 1 tsp urad dal.
Add the fried seasoning to the cooked curry and mix well.
Grate coconut and add it to the contents.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.
note: The dish goes well with rice.

title: Totakoora Kandipapputo
subtitle: Amaranth Leaves Cooked With Toor Dal
procedure: Wash amaranth leaves and finely chop the leaves.
Prepare tamarind puree by soaking tamarind in ½ cup of water.
Add toor dal to the chopped leaves and cook it in a pressure cooker for two whistles or till the toor dal is soft.
Cut onion into thin long pieces and peel the skin off the garlic cloves.
Place a deep frying pan on flame and add oil. Roast mustard seeds, cumin seeds and dried red chillies in the heated oil.
Add onion pieces and garlic cloves to the oil and fry till they turn golden brown in color.
Once cooked, add amaranth leaves to the seasoning and mix well.
Add tamarind puree, salt and turmeric powder to the mixture above. Add ½ cup of water if necessary to get a thin consistency.
Let it cook thoroughly and then put off the flame.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, one spoon of tamarind paste may be used instead of tamarind. 2. This dish goes well with rice and chapattis. 3. Tomatoes can also be used instead of tamarind or tamarind paste.

title: Boppayi Pulusu
subtitle: Semi-Ripened Papaya Soup
procedure: Peel papayas and cut them into big-sized cubes.
Cut okras and drumstick into pieces.
Finely chop Chinese spinach leaves and green chillies.
Add all the vegetables pieces to a thick-bottomed vessel and add water till vegetables float.
Add salt and turmeric powder and let the contents cook on low/medium flame.
Add tamarind puree and jaggery powder to the contents and cook for 5 minutes.
When the vegetables are cooked fully, add besan flour to ½ cup of water and mix it with the contents.
Stir the contents continuously and see that no lumps are formed.
Cook for 5 minutes and put off the flame.
Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies fried in oil in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame as seasoning.
Garnish with finely chopped coriander and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, use 2 cups of tamarind paste.

title: Sorakaya Kootu
subtitle: Bottle Gourd Stew
procedure: Peel bottle gourd and cut them into medium-sized pieces.
Add 3 glasses of water and toor dal to the bottle gourd pieces and cook in a pressure cooker.
Grind coconut, coriander seeds and black pepper in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste.
Add the ground paste to the cooked dal and mix well.
Add salt and curry leaves to the contents and cook for another 2 minutes.
Put off the flame.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the seasoning ingredients and add them to the dal and serve.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Aratidoota Pesarapapputo Koora
subtitle: Banana Stem And Mung Bean Curry

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Cut banana stem into circles. Simultaneously remove the fiber from between the circles by wrapping the fiber around fingers. Discard the fiber.
Chop banana stem circles finely into small pieces — a food processor produces best results.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the pieces of banana stem and mix well.
Squeeze the pieces to completely drain water emanating from them.
Soak Mung Bean for 2 hours in water.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, red dried chillies and cumin seeds.
Add curry leaves, pieces of banana stem and soaked moong dal to the fried seasoning and mix well.
Add ½ cup water to the contents and place a lid over the vessel containing the contents.
Reduce the flame to low and stir the contents frequently.
When the contents are cooked well, add asafoetida and salt to the contents and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. This goes well with rice. 2. Garlic cloves can be added to the seasoning as per taste instead of asafoetida. 3. Grated coconut can also be added to the prepared curry.

title: Bacchali Pappu
subtitle: Chinese Spinach Dal

ingredients.name: Mung Bean green gram dal without skin

procedure: Separate thick stems of Chinese spinach and discard them.
Finely chop the leaves of Chinese spinach and thoroughly wash them.
Add Mung Bean to the chopped leaves and cook on medium flame in a thick bottomed vessel not in a pressure cooker to avoid turning the cooked contents into paste.
Chop tomatoes into small pieces.
Place a thick bottomed pan on flame and pour oil in it.
Roast dried red chillies, mustard seeds, cumin seeds and garlic cloves in the heated oil.
Add green chillies and fry for a minute.
Add tomato pieces, salt and turmeric powder to the seasoning and place a lid over the vessel.
Cook the contents on low flame.
Once tomatoes are cooked, add the cooked dal and mix well.
Let the contents remain on flame for another 5 minutes.
If necessary, add ½ glass of water to the contents to make it into thin consistency.
Garnish the cooked dal with finely chopped coriander leaves and put off the flame.
note: This preparation goes well with rice and chapattis/rotis.

title: Cabbage Pappukoora
subtitle: Cabbage Curry With Mung Bean Or Split Yellow Chick Pea Flour

ingredients.name: Moong dal or split chana dal

procedure: Finely chop cabbage leaves and wash them thoroughly.
Completely drain water from the leaves and add moong or split chana dal.
Add half a glass of water to the contents and cook on low flame in a deep dish — it is preferable not to use a pressure cooker for this recipe.
Add salt to the contents and cook till water gets completely evaporated and the dal is soft.
Place a deep frying pan on medium flame and pour oil.
Roast urad dal, cumin seeds and red dried chilli pieces in the heated oil.
Add the cooked vegetable-dal mixture to the roasted seasoning and mix well.
Add grated coconut to the curry and mix well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. As it takes longer time to cook split chana dal than moong dal, first half-cook chana dal separately in a pan and then add the chopped cabbage leaves to it and cook them together. 2. Usually this curry is a dry one and would not stick to the fingers.

title: Pachivelakkaya Pappu
subtitle: Raw Wood Apple Dal
procedure: Sauté/roast toor dal in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame.
Add water as necessary and cook it in a pressure cooker.
Break wood apple and take out the cream from it.
Add 1 cup of water to the wood apple contents.
Add salt, turmeric powder, green chillies and curry leaves to the content and cook them well.
Mix the cooked toor dal and wood apple contents together.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Add the fried contents to the cooked dal and mix well.
note: The dish should not be too thick. Therefore, add water as necessary while cooking.

title: Vankaya Kootu
subtitle: Eggplants/Aubergine Soup

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Cut eggplants into small pieces and put them in water.
Add water and add eggplant pieces to moong dal and cook well — if cooked in a pressure cooker, one whistle would be sufficient.
Once fully cooked, add grated coconut, curry leaves and salt.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add the fried contents to the cooked curry and mix well.
note: It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Sambar
subtitle: Toor Dal And Vegetable Stew
procedure: Sauté/roast toor dal in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without adding oil.
Add water as necessary and cook it in a pressure cooker.
Cut all the above mentioned vegetables except onions into 1-inch pieces.
Add tamarind puree, turmeric powder and salt to the contents and cook on low/medium flame.
Peel onions and cut them into thin, long pieces.
Fry onions till they turn into golden brown in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame by adding 1 tsp oil.
Add cooked vegetables to the fried onions and cook the contents.
Once cooked, add cooked toor dal to the contents and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry coriander seeds, dried red chillies, fenugreek seeds and split Yellow Chick Pea Flour.
Add coconut pieces and grind the entire fried contents in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste by adding water as necessary.
Add the ground paste to the toor dal and vegetable mixture and cook for another 10 minutes.
Stir the contents and put off the flame.
Garnish Sambar with finely chopped coriander and mustard seeds fried in oil and serve.
note: 1. If tamarind is not available, use 4 cups of tamarind paste. 2. Sautéed/roasted toor dal should be used as it tastes better although sambar can also be prepared without roasting toor dal. 3. Sambar powder can be used instead of using the ground masala.

title: Totakoora Majjigapulusu
subtitle: Amaranth Leaf Stew With Buttermilk
procedure: Finely chop amaranth leaves and wash them.
Mix besan flour to sour buttermilk and keep aside.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the leaves along with one glass of water and cook in a pan/thick bottomed vessel.
Once cooked, add besan flour mixed buttermilk to the cooked amaranth leaves and mix well.
Slit green chillies along their length and add them to the mixture.
Grind coconut into smooth paste and add it to the mixture.
Put the vessel containing the contents on a medium/high flame and cook.
Take a deep frying pan. Add oil and roast dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Pour the roasted seasoning in the cooked contents and put off the flame.
Garnish the contents with finely chopped coriander leaves.
note: 1. This is a very traditional preparation that is good for health and is ideal for those recovering from illness. 2. To make buttermilk sour, leave buttermilk overnight without refrigeration. In cold climates, buttermilk will need to be left in a warm area overnight for it to turn sour.

title: Ullipaya Pulusu
subtitle: Onion Stew
procedure: Peel onions and wash them thoroughly.
Cut green chillies and dried red chillies into 1-inch small pieces.
Cut tomatoes into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add onions and green chillies and fry till onions turn golden brown.
Add tamarind puree, salt, turmeric powder and curry leaves to the fried onions and mix well.
Add cut tomato pieces and jaggery and place a lid over the vessel and cook the contents for 10 minutes.
In a small cup, add rice flour with 1 cup water and make it into thick paste.
Add rice flour paste to the prepared soup and let the contents cook on flame for another 5 minutes.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: 1. If only tamarind paste is available, 50 gm of it may be used. 2. If small-sized onions are available, whole onions may be used.

title: Beerakaya Kootu
subtitle: Ridge Gourd Stew
procedure: Peel ridge gourd and cut into small pieces.
Add toor dal to it and cook by adding ½ glass water.
When fully cooked, add salt to the contents and mix well.
Grind coconut, coriander seeds and black pepper in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste by adding water as necessary.
Add the ground paste to the contents and mix well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 1 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add the fried seasoning and curry leaves to the cooked contents.
Get the stew into a thin consistency by adding water as necessary.
Mix well and cook for ten minutes on low flame.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: This goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Totakoora Avapulusu
subtitle: Amaranth Leaf Stew With Mustard
procedure: Wash Amaranth leaves and finely chop them.
Add tamarind puree, salt, turmeric powder and green chilli pieces to the chopped leaves and cook. Water should be poured in such a way that it should float above the chopped amaranth leaves.
Once cooked, mix rice flour in half a cup of water and add to the soup of cooked leaves.
Cook the rice flour mixed contents for 5 minutes on a medium flame.
In a food processor/grinder/mixie, grind mustard seeds by adding water as necessary and make it into smooth paste.
Add the ground mustard paste to the soup.
Place a deep frying pan on flame with oil.
When oil is heated, roast fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies.
Add chilli powder to the roasted seasoning and fry for a minute and pour the contents into the soup and mix well.
note: This dish goes well with rice.

title: Vankaya Pulusu Pachadi
subtitle: Eggplant Stew
procedure: Apply oil to the outer skin of the eggplants, directly place them whole on low flame and roast.
Once completely roasted and the eggplant is soft, put off the flame.
Peel the skin of eggplants and grind the fried eggplants into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie.
Add tamarind puree to the ground paste.
Peel onions and chop them into fine pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add onions and green chillies to the fried contents and fry till onions turn into golden brown.
Put off the flame and add the fried contents to the prepared tamarind puree mixed with eggplant paste.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the prepared eggplant stew and mix well.
note: If tamarind is not available, add 2 tsp of tamarind paste.

title: Tomato Stew
subtitle: Tomato Stew
procedure: Peel onions and cut them into small pieces.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies.
Add onions and fry them till they turn into golden brown.
Add tomatoes, green chillies, tamarind puree, jaggery, turmeric powder and salt to the contents and cook them well.
Once cooked, add besan flour mixed in ½ cup water to the contents and mix well.
Cook the contents for 5 minutes and put off the flame.

title: Mamidikaya Pulusu
subtitle: Semi Ripe Mangoes Stew
procedure: Peel mangoes and cut them into small pieces.
Add water till mango pieces float above it.
Add salt, turmeric powder, asafoetida, green chillies, curry leaves and jaggery and cook the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add red chilli powder and fry for 1 second.
Put off the flame and add the fried contents to the soup.
Mix rice flour in ½ cup of water and add the contents to the soup and cook the soup for 1 minute.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: It goes well with rice.

title: Mamidikaya Pappu
subtitle: Raw Mangoes Dal
procedure: Sauté/roast toor dal in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame.
Add water as necessary to the fried dal and cook in a pressure cooker.
Peel mangoes and cut into small pieces.
Add water till mango pieces float above the water.
Add salt, turmeric powder, green chillies and curry leaves and cook the contents.
Once fully cooked, add toor dal and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, cumin seeds and asafoetida or garlic cloves.
Add red chilli powder to the contents and fry for 1 second.
Put off the flame and add the fried contents to the cooked dal and serve.
note: The same method can be followed while preparing the dish with moong dal.

title: Pachicharu
subtitle: Uncooked Rasam
procedure: Thin the puree with water.
Add jaggery powder, salt and turmeric powder and mix the contents well.
Finely chop green chillies and coriander leaves and add them to the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Add the fried content to the prepared charu.
note: It is not required to boil the charu. (*charu = soup)

title: Chintakaya Pulusu
subtitle: Tender Green Tamarind Soup
procedure: Wash and cut tamarind into 2 inch pieces. Add water to them and cook.
Once cooked, keep the contents aside and let it cool.
Once cooled, squeeze the contents using hands and separate seeds and skin from it.
Strain the contents using a strainer.
Peel bottle gourd and cut it into 2 inch pieces.
Add 3 cups of water to the tamarind pulp along with salt, green chillies, turmeric powder and bottle gourd pieces.
Place the vessel containing the contents on low/medium flame.
Place a frying pan on low/medium flame and fry few mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Add red chilli powder to the contents and put off the flame.
Add the fried contents to the pulusu and mix the contents well.
Add rice flour in ½ cup of water and add it to the pulusu and let the contents cook for 5 minutes.
Grind the remaining mustard seeds in a food processor/mixie into smooth paste by adding water as necessary.
Put off the flame.
Add the ground paste to the contents and mix the contents.
Garnish pulusu with chopped coriander.
note: * pulusu : soup

title: Chintachiguru Pappu
subtitle: Dal With Tender Shoots Of Tamarind Tree

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Cook moong dal on low/medium flame by adding water as necessary.
Squeeze tender shoots of tamarind tree to remove the stalks from them.
Add water to the tender shoots along with salt, turmeric powder, green chillies and curry leaves and cook the contents.
Mix cooked tender shoots of tamarind tree and moong dal together.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida.
Add red chilli powder to the contents and fry for 1 minute.
Put off the flame and mix the fried contents to the cooked contents and serve.
note: Instead of asafoetida, garlic cloves can be used.

title: Boodidagummadi Majjigapulusu
subtitle: Ash Gourd And Buttermilk Stew
procedure: Peel ash gourd and cut it into 1-inch pieces.
Add salt to the cut pieces and cook till the pieces turn soft.
Grind coconut, green chillies and coriander seeds together into smooth paste adding water as necessary.
Add besan flour to the smooth paste and mix it in the buttermilk.
Put the buttermilk on low flame, add cooked ash gourd pieces, and cook again for another 5 minutes.
Place a deep frying pan on low flame with 1 tsp oil and when hot, fry mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida and red dried chillies in it.
Pour the fried seasoning on the prepared buttermilk soup.
Garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves and mix well.

title: Bacchalipulusu
subtitle: Chinese Spinach Stew
procedure: Finely chop Chinese spinach leaves and wash them thoroughly.
In a vessel, add the chopped Chinese spinach leaves, salt, turmeric powder and tamarind paste and put it on low/medium flame.
Slit green chillies into half along its length and add them to the contents.
Add asafoetida to the contents while cooking.
Once cooked, add rice flour mixed in ½ cup water and pour it into the contents.
Mix the contents well. Let the contents remain on flame for 2 minutes and put off the flame.
Add small quantity of water as necessary and grind mustard seeds into a smooth paste. Add mustard paste to the cooked contents and mix well.
Remove the stew from flame.
In another deep frying pan, roast fenugreek seeds and red dried chilli pieces in 2 tsp oil and pour it into the stew.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.
note: Do not cook after adding mustard paste, as stew may turn bitter.

title: Aratipuvvu Pappukoora
subtitle: Banana Flower And Mung Bean Curry

ingredients.name: Moong dal/mung bean green gram without skin

procedure: Nip the pedicels and stalks off the banana flower and wash it thoroughly.
Grind banana flowers coarsely in a food processor/mixie.
Wash the ground flowers in a strainer using water.
Completely drain the water from the ground flowers by squeezing it and keep aside the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry urad dal, cumin seeds and red dried chilli pieces.
Add curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry for 1 minute.
Add ground banana flower and Mung Bean and add ½ glass of water to the contents.
Mix the contents well and place a lid over the vessel containing the contents.
Reduce flame to low and stir the contents frequently from time-to-time.
When dal is cooked, add asafoetida and salt.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.

title: Mullangi Pesarapappukoora
subtitle: Radish And Mung Bean Curry

ingredients.name: Mung Bean green gram without skin

procedure: Soak Mung Bean for 2 hours in water.
Wash radish thoroughly. Peel it and finely grate it in a food processor/mixie.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry red dried chilli pieces, urad dal and cumin seeds.
Add curry leaves to the fried seasoning and fry for 2 minutes.
Add radish to the seasoning. Drain water completely from the Mung Bean and add to the radish. Add ½ cup water to the contents.
Place a lid over the vessel and pour water over the lid — ½ cup of water poured over the lid prevents the contents from sticking to the sides of the pan.
When radish is cooked soft, add salt and grated coconut.
Mix the contents well and put off the flame.
note: A pinch of asafoetida can be added to this depending on taste.

title: Dosakaya Pappu
subtitle: Yellow Cucumber Dal
procedure: Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and sauté/roast toor dal without adding oil.
When roasted, add two cups of water and cook in a pressure cooker.
Peel cucumber and cut it into small pieces. Indian cucumbers are sometimes bitter — take a small piece and taste it to check for bitterness. If bitter, discard and use another one.
In a thick-bottomed vessel add the cut cucumber pieces, salt, turmeric powder, tamarind puree, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add 1 glass of water to the contents and cook them on low/medium flame.
When the contents are cooked, add the cooked toor dal and mix the contents well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, cumin seeds, mustard seeds and asafoetida.
Add the fried contents to the cooked dal.
note: 1. If tamarind is not available, use 2 tsp of tamarind paste. 2. Add water as necessary to make the consistency of the dish in such a way that it is neither too thin nor too thick. 3. If garlic is used, fry it in heated oil and add to the dal at the end.

title: Kakarakaya Paccipulusu
subtitle: Bitter Gourd Stew
procedure: Wash bitter gourds thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 4 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, add bitter gourd pieces and salt and place a lid over the contents.
Reduce the flame to low and fry the contents for ½ an hour, stirring frequently.
Add tamarind puree, grated jaggery, and turmeric powder to the contents and mix well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add 2 tsp oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Add the fried contents and red chilli powder to the bitter gourd pieces and mix the contents well.
Put off the flame and serve.
note: If tamarind is not available, add 1 cup of tamarind paste.

title: Andhra Mukkala Pulusu Dhappalam
subtitle: Traditional Andhra Vegetable Stew
procedure: Wash all vegetables thoroughly. Cut all the above mentioned vegetables into a thick-bottomed vessel and add salt, turmeric powder, asafoetida, tamarind puree, jaggery and green chillies.
Place this vessel on low/medium flame and cook the contents.
Add water as necessary along with tamarind puree so that the stew is a thin consistency. See that the vegetables are completely covered in the water even as they cook.
Stir the contents frequently.
When the vegetables are cooked, pour besan flour mixed in half-a cup of water to the soup and mix well.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry asafoetida, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies.
Add the fried seasoning to the stew and put off the flame.
Garnish the stew with finely chopped coriander leaves.
note: 1. It goes well with dal — a thick purée of pulses. This is usually prepared during marriage ceremonies and other such auspicious occasions. 2. This stew can also be prepared using bottle gourd instead of pumpkin. 3. If tamarind is not available, use 5 cups of tamarind paste.

title: Gongoora Pulusu
subtitle: Sorrel Leaf Stew
procedure: Clean sorrel leaves of stalks. Finely chop the leaves into small pieces and wash them thoroughly.
Peel bottle gourd and cut them into 2-inch pieces.
Peel garlic and keep aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
When it crackles, add garlic cloves to the contents and fry for ½ minute.
Put off the flame and keep the contents aside.
Place a thick-bottomed vessel on low/medium flame and add bottle gourd pieces, sorrel leaves, turmeric powder, chilli powder, and salt.
Add water till the contents are fully covered and cook the contents.
Once fully cooked, add the fried seasoning and rice flour mixed in ½ cup water to the contents and mix well.
Cook the contents for 2 minutes and put off the flame.
note: This can be stored for 2-3 days without refrigeration.

title: Tamata Pappu
subtitle: Tomato Dal
procedure: Sauté/roast toor dal in a deep frying pan on low/medium flame without adding oil.
Add water as necessary and cook it in a pressure cooker.
Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Add salt, turmeric powder and green chillies to it and cook them well.
Add cooked toor dal to the contents and cook for 5 minutes.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, semi-fry mustard seeds, cumin seeds and dried red chillies.
Add garlic cloves to the contents and fry for 1 minute.
Add the fried contents to the cooked dal.
Garnish the cooked dal with finely chopped coriander and serve.
note: 1. This goes well with rice and chapattis. 2. Same method can be followed while preparing the dish with Mung Bean except that the Mung Bean need not be roasted.

title: Tomato Soup
subtitle: Tomato Soup
procedure: Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
Add water till tomatoes are covered fully.
Add salt and cook the contents well.
Put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Grind tomatoes into smooth paste and strain to remove seeds and the skin from the juice.
Grind ginger into smooth paste and strain it along with tomato juice in a strainer.
Put the vessel containing tomato juice on low/medium flame and cook the contents well.
Add black pepper powder and sugar to the contents while hot and serve with croutons.

title: Tamata Perugu Pachadi
subtitle: Tomato Raita
procedure: Wash tomatoes thoroughly and cut them into pieces.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies and mustard seeds.
Add tomatoes, turmeric powder and salt to the contents.
Place a lid over the vessel containing the contents — do not add water.
Reduce the flame and cook well.
Once cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Add the cooled contents to curd/yogurt.
Finely chop green chillies and coriander leaves and mix them well with the contents.
note: 1. This goes well with rice, chapattis and Idlies. 2. Do not add cooked tomatoes to curd/yogurt when hot as curd may turn sour. Add only when the contents are cooled.

title: Totakoora Perugu Pachadi
subtitle: Amaranth Leaves Raita
procedure: Finely chop amaranth leaves and wash thoroughly.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the chopped leaves and cook with ½ cup water in a thick-bottomed pan on low/medium flame.
Place a deep frying pan on flame with oil.
Once oil is heated, roast mustard seeds and dried red chillies. Put off the flame.
Add curd to the seasoning and mix well.
Completely drain water from the cooked amaranth leaves after it is cooled and add to the curd.
Add coriander leaves and split green chillies to the curd and mix well.
note: This dish goes well with chapattis.

title: Boodidagummadi Perugu Pachadi
subtitle: Ash Gourd Raita
procedure: Peel ash gourd, grate it, and add to the curd/yogurt.
Finely chop onions, tomatoes and coriander leaves and add to the curd/yogurt.
Add salt to the curd/yogurt and mix well.
For seasoning, fry mustard seeds in heated oil. When spluttering, pour it into the curd/yogurt and mix well.
Finely chop green chillies and add to the mixture and serve.
note: 1. This goes well with chapattis. 2. This is also known as ash gourd raita.

title: Aratidoota Perugupachadi
subtitle: Banana Stem Raita
procedure: Cut banana stem into circles. Simultaneously remove the fiber from between the circles by wrapping the fiber around fingers. Discard the fiber.
Chop banana stem circles finely into small pieces — a food processor produces best results.
Add salt and turmeric powder to the pieces of banana stem and mix well.
Squeeze the pieces to completely drain water emanating from them.
Grind mustard seeds into smooth paste in a food processor/mixie by adding water as necessary.
Chop green chillies and dried red chillies into small pieces and keep them aside.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame with oil.
When oil is heated, fry red dried chillies, mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and pour the contents onto the curd/yoghurt.
Add chopped green chillies and coriander leaves to the curd/yoghurt.
Add pieces of banana stem to the contents and mix well.
Add mustard paste to the contents and mix well.
note: For preparing this dish, uncooked pieces of banana stem should be used. Banana stem is an excellent source of fiber for all and is particularly recommended for diabetics.

title: Boodida Gummadikaya Raita
subtitle: Ash Gourd Raita
procedure: Peel ash gourd and grate it.
Finely chop tomatoes and onions into small pieces.
Add the contents to curd/yogurt and add salt to the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds and dried red chillies gently break them into pieces.
Add the fried seasoning to the curd/yogurt and serve.
note: Ash gourd is said to be good for health.

title: Sorakaya Perugupachadi
subtitle: Bottle Gourd Raita
procedure: Peel bottle gourd and cut them into ½-inch pieces.
Add salt and water as necessary and cook the contents on low/medium flame.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and let the contents cool.
Finely chop green chillies and coriander leaves and add them to the curd/yogurt.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry the seasoning ingredients and add them to the curd/yogurt.
Add the cooked bottle gourd contents to the curd/yogurt and mix the contents well.
note: 1. As per taste, add grated coconut to the contents. 2. It goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Menthikoora Pappu
subtitle: Fenugreek Leaf Dal
procedure: Remove stalks of fenugreek leaves and finely chop them into pieces. Wash them thoroughly and keep aside.
Cook toor dal with water in a pressure cooker till dal is soft.
Once cooked, add fenugreek leaves and tomatoes and cook the contents on low/medium flame.
When fully cooked, put off the flame and add salt to the contents and mix well.
If the dal is too thick, add water as necessary and cook till a thin consistency is obtained.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry mustard seeds, dried red chillies and cumin seeds.
Add garlic cloves to the fried seasoning and fry till they turn into golden brown.
Add the fried seasoning to the cooked dal and garnish the contents with finely chopped coriander leaves.
note: This goes well with rice and chapattis.

title: Boppayi Pappu
subtitle: Raw Papaya Dal

ingredients.name: Mung Bean green gram without skin

procedure: Peel papaya and wash it thoroughly. Cut it into small pieces.
Add Mung Bean and ½ cup water to the contents and cook — do not cook in a pressure cooker, as this may turn the contents into smooth paste.
Add asafoetida to the contents while cooking.
Add salt to the contents and put off the flame.
Add the fried seasoning of dried red chillies, urad dal and garlic cloves to the contents and serve.

title: Mullangi Perugupachadi
subtitle: Radish Raita
procedure: Wash and peel radish and carrot and grate them. Add grated pieces to curd/yogurt.
Finely chop tomatoes, onions and coriander leaves and add them to curd/yoghurt.
Add salt to the curd/yoghurt and serve.
note: 1. This goes well with chapattis. 2. It can also be eaten as a stand-alone dish. 3. This is very good for health.

title: Menthi Majjiga
subtitle: Buttermilk With Fenugreek Seeds
procedure: Add salt and turmeric powder to buttermilk.
Finely chop green chillies and coriander leaves and add them to the contents.
Place a deep frying pan on low/medium flame and add oil to it.
When oil is heated, fry dried red chillies, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and ajwan and add them to the contents.
note: 1. Fermented buttermilk is not fit for consumption. 2. Hence try to use sour buttermilk to avoid wastage and also for better flavor.
